# Refresh EVE Online access tokens using refresh tokens
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

TOKENS_PATH = os.path.expanduser("~/.openclaw/eve-tokens.json")


def retrieve_tokens():
    if not os.path.exists(TOKENS_PATH):
        print(f"ERROR: Tokens file missing: {TOKENS_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Execute auth_flow.py initially for authentication.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    with open(TOKENS_PATH) as file:
        return json.load(file)


def update_access_token(refresh_token, client_id):
    payload = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "grant_type": "refresh_token",
        "refresh_token": refresh_token,
        "client_id": client_id,
    }).encode()
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://login.eveonline.com/v2/oauth/token",
        data=payload,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
        method="POST",
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
            return json.loads(response.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        content = error.read().decode()
        print(f"ERROR: Token renewal failed ({error.code}): {content}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


def persist_tokens(data):
    with open(TOKENS_PATH, "w") as file:
        json.dump(data, file, indent=2)
    os.chmod(TOKENS_PATH, 0o600)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Acquire a new EVE ESI access token")
    parser.add_argument("--char", default="primary",
                        help="Character identifier to utilize (default: primary)")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true",
                        help="Display complete token response in JSON format")
    parser.add_argument("--show", action="store_true",
                        help="Display all saved characters")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()

    tokens = retrieve_tokens()
    characters = tokens.get("characters", {})

    if arguments.show:
        if not characters:
            print("No characters recorded. Run auth_flow.py first.")
            return
        for label, char in characters.items():
            print(f"  {label}: {char.get('character_name')} (ID: {char.get('character_id')})")
        return

    if arguments.char not in characters:
        print(f"ERROR: Character '{arguments.char}' not located.", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Available: {', '.join(characters.keys()) or 'none'}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Run auth_flow.py --char-name <name> to authenticate.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    character = characters[arguments.char]
    token_info = update_access_token(character["refresh_token"], character["client_id"])

    # Update stored refresh_token (EVE changes it after each refresh)
    if "refresh_token" in token_info:
        characters[arguments.char]["refresh_token"] = token_info["refresh_token"]
        persist_tokens(tokens)

    if arguments.json:
        print(json.dumps(token_info, indent=2))
    else:
        print(token_info["access_token"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as patches
import torch
from pathlib import Path
from argparse import ArgumentParser
import sys
import heapq

# Extend system path to include local modules
sys.path.extend(
    [Path(__file__).parent.as_posix(), Path(__file__).parents[2].as_posix()]
)
from paroquant_kernels import scaled_pairwise_rotation
from paroquant.optim.qlinear import PseudoQuantizedLinear
# Initialize plotting configurations
from plot_init import *

# Set up argument parser
parser = ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument(
    "--optimized-state-path",
    required=True,
    type=str,
    help="Location of the optimized linear layer state dictionary.",
)
parser.add_argument(
    "--q_group_size",
    default=128,
    type=int,
    help="Quantization group size.",
)
parser.add_argument(
    "--save-dir",
    default="figures",
    type=str,
    help="Directory where the generated figure will be stored.",
)
parser.add_argument("--plot_index", default=0, type=int)
arguments = parser.parse_args()

print("Loading optimized results...")
state_dict = torch.load(arguments.optimized_state_path, map_location="cuda")
quant_layer = PseudoQuantizedLinear.from_state_dict(state_dict)
original_weight = quant_layer.weight.detach()

print("Computing original and rotated weights...")
rotated_weight = quant_layer.weight.detach()
rotated_weight = rotated_weight * quant_layer.channel_scales
rotated_weight = scaled_pairwise_rotation(
    rotated_weight, quant_layer.pairs_grouped, quant_layer.angles_grouped
)

print("Identifying top correlated channel pairs...")
grouped_weight = original_weight.view(original_weight.shape[0], -1, arguments.q_group_size).permute(1, 0, 2)
top_count = 5
priority_queue = []

for rotation_idx in range(quant_layer.pairs_grouped.shape[0]):
    pair_list = quant_layer.pairs_grouped[rotation_idx].reshape(-1, 2).cpu()
    # Adjust indices based on group position
    for start_idx in range(0, original_weight.shape[1], arguments.q_group_size):
        pair_list[start_idx : start_idx + arguments.q_group_size] += start_idx
    
    for idx1, idx2 in pair_list:
        vec_i = rotated_weight[:, idx1]
        vec_j = rotated_weight[:, idx2]
        
        # Ensure vec_i corresponds to higher variance channel
        if original_weight[:, idx1].var() < original_weight[:, idx2].var():
            vec_i, vec_j = vec_j, vec_i
            idx1, idx2 = idx2, idx1
        
        correlation = torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([vec_i, vec_j]))[0, 1].item()
        
        if len(priority_queue) < top_count:
            heapq.heappush(priority_queue, (correlation, (idx1.item(), idx2.item())))
        else:
            if correlation > priority_queue[0][0]:
                heapq.heapreplace(priority_queue, (correlation, (idx1.item(), idx2.item())))

# Sort top-k pairs by correlation descending
top_pairs = sorted(priority_queue, key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)

# Print top correlations
for corr, (idx1, idx2) in top_pairs:
    print(f"Channel pair ({idx1}, {idx2}) -> correlation={corr:.6f}")

# Select specific pair based on provided index
selected_i, selected_j = top_pairs[arguments.plot_index][1]

# Extract relevant channels

import torch
from torch import nn
from src.audio2pose_models.cvae import CVAE
from src.audio2pose_models.discriminator import PoseSequenceDiscriminator
from src.audio2pose_models.audio_encoder import AudioEncoder

class Audio2Pose(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config, wav2lip_ckpt_path, device='cuda'):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.sequence_length = config.MODEL.CVAE.SEQ_LEN
        self.latent_size = config.MODEL.CVAE.LATENT_SIZE
        self.device = device
        
        # Initialize and freeze audio encoder
        self.audio_enc = AudioEncoder(wav2lip_ckpt_path, device)
        self.audio_enc.eval()
        for param in self.audio_enc.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False
            
        # Initialize generator and discriminator
        self.generator = CVAE(config)
        self.motion_discriminator = PoseSequenceDiscriminator(config)

    def forward(self, input_data):
        batch = {}
        
        # Process ground truth coefficients
        gt_coeff = input_data['gt'].to(self.device).squeeze(0)           # bs (frame_len+1) 73
        batch['pose_motion_gt'] = gt_coeff[:, 1:, 64:70] - gt_coeff[:, :1, 64:70]  # bs frame_len 6
        batch['reference'] = gt_coeff[:, 0, 64:70]                      # bs 6
        batch['class_label'] = input_data['class'].squeeze(0).to(self.device)      # bs
        batch['audio_features'] = input_data['indiv_mels'].to(self.device).squeeze(0)  # bs seq_len+1 80 16
        
        # Extract audio embeddings
        audio_emb = self.audio_enc(batch['audio_features'][:, 1:, :, :].unsqueeze(2))  # bs seq_len 512
        batch['audio_emb'] = audio_emb
        
        # Generate pose motion
        batch = self.generator(batch)
        batch['pose_pred'] = batch['reference'].unsqueeze(1) + batch['pose_motion_pred']  # bs frame_len 6
        batch['pose_gt'] = gt_coeff[:, 1:, 64:70].clone()                                # bs frame_len 6
        
        return batch
    
    def test(self, input_batch):
        batch = {}
        
        # Prepare reference pose and class info
        ref_pose = input_batch['ref']                            # bs 1 70
        batch['reference'] = ref_pose[:, 0, -6:]  
        batch['class_label'] = input_batch['class']  
        batch_size = ref_pose.shape[0]
        
        # Prepare audio features
        audio_mels = input_batch['indiv_mels']                   # bs T 1 80 16
        audio_input = audio_mels[:, 1:]                          # we treat the ref as first frame
        num_frames = int(input_batch['num_frames']) - 1
        
        # Process in chunks of sequence length
        full_chunks = num_frames // self.sequence_length
        remainder = num_frames % self.sequence_length
        
        motion_predictions = [torch.zeros((batch_size, 1, 6), dtype=ref_pose.dtype, 
                                          device=ref_pose.device)]
        
        for i in range(full_chunks):
            z = torch.randn(batch_size, self.latent_size).to(ref_pose.device)
            batch['z'] = z
            audio_emb = self.audio_enc(audio_input[:, i*self.sequence_length:(i+1)*self.sequence_length,:,:,:])
            batch['audio_emb'] = audio_emb
            batch = self.generator.test(batch)
            motion_predictions.append(batch['pose_motion_pred'])
        
        # Handle remaining frames
        if remainder != 0:
            z = torch.randn(batch_size, self.latent_size).to(ref_pose.device)
            batch['z'] = z
            audio_emb = self.audio_enc(audio_input[:, -1*self.sequence_length:,:,:,:])
            
            # Pad if necessary
            if audio_emb.shape[1] != self.sequence_length:
                pad_len = self.sequence_length - audio_emb.shape[1]
                padded_audio = audio_emb[:, :1].repeat(1, pad_len, 1)
                audio_emb = torch.cat([padded_audio, audio_emb], dim=1)
                
            batch['audio_emb'] = audio_emb
            batch = self.generator.test(batch)
            motion_predictions.append(batch['pose_motion_pred'][:, -1*remainder:, :])
        
        # Combine all motion predictions
        batch['pose_motion_pred'] = torch.cat(motion_predictions, dim=1)
        batch['pose_pred'] = ref_pose[:, :1, -6:] + batch['pose_motion_pred']
        
        return batch

def is_right_triangle(x, y, z):
    '''
    Given the lengths of the three sides of a triangle. Return True if the three
    sides form a right-angled triangle, False otherwise.
    A right-angled triangle is a triangle in which one angle is right angle or 
    90 degree.
    Example:
    is_right_triangle(3, 4, 5) == True
    is_right_triangle(1, 2, 3) == False
    '''
    tolerance = 1e-9
    x_sq = x * x
    y_sq = y * y
    z_sq = z * z
    
    if abs(x_sq + y_sq - z_sq) < tolerance:
        return True
    if abs(x_sq + z_sq - y_sq) < tolerance:
        return True
    if abs(y_sq + z_sq - x_sq) < tolerance:
        return True
    
    return False

def gen_composed_video(args, device, first_frame_coeff, coeff_path, audio_path, save_path, exp_dim=64):
    
    # Load coefficient data from mat files
    initial_coeff = scio.loadmat(first_frame_coeff)['full_3dmm']
    predicted_coeff = scio.loadmat(coeff_path)['coeff_3dmm']
    
    # Construct full coefficient matrix by combining initial and predicted coefficients
    full_coeff = np.repeat(initial_coeff, predicted_coeff.shape[0], axis=0)  # 257 dimensions
    full_coeff[:, 80:144] = predicted_coeff[:, 0:64]
    full_coeff[:, 224:227] = predicted_coeff[:, 64:67]  # 3 dim translation
    full_coeff[:, 254:] = predicted_coeff[:, 67:]  # 3 dim translation
    
    temp_video_file = '/tmp/face3dtmp.mp4'
    face_model = FaceReconModel(args)
    
    # Initialize video writer
    output_video = cv2.VideoWriter(temp_video_file, cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*'mp4v'), 25, (224, 224))
    
    # Process each frame
    for idx in tqdm(range(predicted_coeff.shape[0]), 'face3d rendering:'):
        current_coeff = torch.tensor(full_coeff[idx:idx+1], device=device)
        face_model.forward(current_coeff, device)
        
        # Get landmark predictions
        landmark_pred = face_model.pred_lm
        landmark_pred = landmark_pred.cpu().numpy().squeeze()
        
        # Get rendered face image
        rendered_image = face_model.pred_face
        rendered_image = 255. * rendered_image.cpu().numpy().squeeze().transpose(1, 2, 0)
        
        # Prepare output frame
        frame_img = rendered_image[:, :, :3].astype(np.uint8)
        output_video.write(np.uint8(frame_img[:, :, ::-1]))
    
    output_video.release()
    
    # Merge audio and video using ffmpeg
    merge_command = 'ffmpeg -v quiet -y -i {} -i {} -strict -2 -q:v 1 {}'.format(audio_path, temp_video_file, save_path)
    subprocess.call(merge_command, shell=platform.system() != 'Windows')

def check_file_exists(name):
    """Determine if a specific file exists"""
    global METRIC_PREFIX
    # Remove the predefined prefix from the metric name
    clean_name = name.replace(METRIC_PREFIX,"")
    
    # Convert underscore-separated path to actual filesystem path
    filepath = "/" + clean_name.replace("_present","").replace("_","/")
    
    # Return 1 if file exists, otherwise 0
    if os.path.isfile(filepath):
        return 1
    else:
        return 0

def retrieve_file_size(name):
    """Get the size of a specified file in bytes"""
    global METRIC_PREFIX
    # Strip the metric prefix from the name
    clean_name = name.replace(METRIC_PREFIX,"")
    # Construct the file path
    filepath = "/" + clean_name.replace("_size","").replace("_","/")
    try:
        # Return file size using os.stat
        return os.stat(filepath).st_size
    except OSError:
        # Return 0 if file doesn't exist or is inaccessible
        return 0

    desc = base.copy()
    for key, value in properties.iteritems():

def convert_number_system(number: int, target_base: int):
    """Convert a decimal number to a different base representation.
    Returns the string representation in the new base.
    The target base is guaranteed to be less than 10.
    >>> convert_number_system(8, 3)
    '22'
    >>> convert_number_system(8, 2)
    '1000'
    >>> convert_number_system(7, 2)
    '111'
    """
    if number == 0:
        return '0'
    converted = ''
    while number > 0:
        converted = str(number % target_base) + converted
        number //= target_base
    return converted

# Handle errors from Volcengine API calls
def process_volcengine_exception(exc: Exception) -> Exception:
    """Process Volcengine API exceptions
    Args:
        exc: The exception that was raised during API call
    Returns:
        Normalized ClientError containing Volcengine error information
    """
    # Default handling for unclassified exceptions
    return ClientError(f'An error occurred: {str(exc)}')

class ClientError(Exception):
    """Represents a client-side error indicating the request was invalid or malformed."""
    def __init__(self, msg):
        """Initialize ClientError with message."""
        # Invoke parent class constructor with required arguments
        super().__init__(msg)
        self.category = 'client'
        self.description = msg

class ServerError(Exception):
    """Represents a server-side error indicating a problem in request processing."""
    def __init__(self, description: str):
        """Initialize ServerError with description."""
        super().__init__(description)
        self.category = 'server'
        self.description = description

# Translate characters using two character sets
from ..process import Process
from ..command_decorators import command
from . import register_command

@command()
@register_command('tr')
def cmd_translate(process: Process) -> int:
    """
    Translate characters from one set to another
    Usage: tr set1 set2
    """
    if len(process.arguments) < 2:
        process.stderr.write("tr: missing operand\n")
        return 1
    
    input_set = process.arguments[0].encode('utf-8')
    output_set = process.arguments[1].encode('utf-8')
    
    if len(input_set) != len(output_set):
        process.stderr.write("tr: sets must be same length\n")
        return 1
    
    # Build translation mapping
    translation_table = bytes.maketrans(input_set, output_set)
    
    # Read input data and apply translation
    raw_data = process.stdin.read()
    result = raw_data.translate(translation_table)
    
    process.stdout.write(result)
    return 0

# Convert FP8 weights to BF16 format using Triton for dequantization
import json
import os
from argparse import ArgumentParser
from glob import glob
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl
from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file
from tqdm import tqdm

@triton.jit
def dequantize_weight_kernel(input_ptr, scale_ptr, output_ptr, rows, cols, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr):
    block_row = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    block_col = tl.program_id(axis=1)
    num_blocks_per_col = tl.cdiv(cols, BLOCK_SIZE)
    row_indices = block_row * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
    col_indices = block_col * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
    indices = row_indices[:, None] * cols + col_indices[None, :]
    valid_mask = (row_indices[:, None] < rows) & (col_indices[None, :] < cols)
    data = tl.load(input_ptr + indices, mask=valid_mask).to(tl.float32)
    scale_value = tl.load(scale_ptr + block_row * num_blocks_per_col + block_col)
    result = data * scale_value
    tl.store(output_ptr + indices, result, mask=valid_mask)

def dequantize_weights(input_tensor: torch.Tensor, scales: torch.Tensor, block_dim: int = 128) -> torch.Tensor:
    assert input_tensor.is_contiguous() and scales.is_contiguous()
    assert input_tensor.dim() == 2 and scales.dim() == 2
    M, N = input_tensor.shape
    output = torch.empty_like(input_tensor, dtype=torch.get_default_dtype())
    
    def compute_grid(meta):
        return (triton.cdiv(M, meta["BLOCK_SIZE"]), triton.cdiv(N, meta["BLOCK_SIZE"]))
    
    dequantize_weight_kernel[compute_grid](input_tensor, scales, output, M, N, BLOCK_SIZE=block_dim)
    return output

def process_model(fp8_directory, bf16_directory):
    torch.set_default_dtype(torch.bfloat16)
    os.makedirs(bf16_directory, exist_ok=True)
    os.system("cp -rf " + fp8_directory + "/config.json " + bf16_directory)
    os.system("cp -rf " + fp8_directory + "/*.py " + bf16_directory)
    os.system("cp -rf " + fp8_directory + "/tokenizer* " + bf16_directory)
    os.system("cp -rf " + fp8_directory + "/chat_template* " + bf16_directory)
    
    index_file = os.path.join(fp8_directory, "model.safetensors.index.json")
    with open(index_file) as f:
        model_index_data = json.load(f)
    weight_mapping = model_index["weight_map"]
    
    # Cache for loaded safetensor files
    cached_files = {}
    processed_fp8_names = []
    
    # Helper function to retrieve tensor from appropriate file
    def fetch_tensor(tensor_identifier):
        source_file = weight_mapping[tensor_identifier]
        if source_file not in cached_files:
            full_path = os.path.join(fp8_directory, source_file)
            cached_files[source_file] = load_file(full_path, device="cuda")
        return cached_files[source_file][tensor_identifier]
    
    safetensor_list = list(glob(os.path.join(fp8_directory, "*.safetensors")))
    safetensor_list.sort()
    
    for current_file in tqdm(safetensor_list):
        print(f"Processing file: {current_file}")
        filename = os.path.basename(current_file)
        current_tensors = load_file(current_file, device="cuda")
        cached_files[filename] = current_tensors
        
        updated_state = {}
        for weight_key, weight_value in current_tensors.items():
            if weight_key.endswith("_scale_inv"):
                continue
            elif weight_value.element_size() == 1:  # FP8 precision weight
                scale_inverse_key = f"{weight_key}_scale_inv"
                try:
                    # Retrieve scale inverse from correct file
                    inv_scale = fetch_tensor(scale_inverse_key)
                    processed_fp8_names.append(weight_key)
                    updated_state[weight_key] = dequantize_weights(weight_value, inv_scale)
                except KeyError:
                    print(f"Warning: Missing scale_inv for {weight_key}, skipping conversion")
                    updated_state[weight_key] = weight_value
            else:
                updated_state[weight_key] = weight_value
        
        new_output_path = os.path.join(bf16_directory, filename)
        save_file(updated_state, new_output_path)
        
        # Memory optimization: retain only two most recently accessed files
        if len(cached_files) > 2:
            first_key = next(iter(cached_files))
            del cached_files[first_key]
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    
    # Update model index
    updated_index_path = os.path.join(bf16_directory, "model.safetensors.index.json")
    for weight_name in processed_fp8_names:
        scale_inv_key = f"{weight_name}_scale_inv"
        if scale_inv_key in weight_mapping:
            weight_mapping.pop(scale_inv_key)
    
    with open(updated_index_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"metadata": {}, "weight_map": weight_mapping}, f, indent=2)

    parser = ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--input-fp8-hf-path", type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output-bf16-hf-path", type=str, required=True)
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    process_model(arguments.input_fp8_hf_path, arguments.output_bf16_hf_path)

# Calculate world offsets for arranging multiple simulation worlds in a grid layout
from typing import Any
import numpy as np
import warp as wp
from ..core.types import Axis
from .download_assets import clear_git_cache, download_asset
from .texture import load_texture, normalize_texture
from .topology import topological_sort, topological_sort_undirected

def check_conditional_support():
    """
    Determine whether conditional graph execution is supported in the current environment.
    Returns:
        bool: True if conditional graphs are supported, False otherwise.
    """
    return wp.is_conditional_graph_supported()

def compute_world_positions(num_worlds: int, cell_size: tuple[float, float, float], vertical_axis: Any = None):
    """
    Calculate 3D position offsets for organizing multiple worlds in a structured grid.
    
    This function arranges worlds in a grid pattern based on the provided spacing (cell_size).
    The dimensionality of the grid is inferred from non-zero entries in cell_size.
    
    Args:
        num_worlds: Number of worlds to position.
        cell_size: Spacing between adjacent worlds along each axis. Non-zero values define active dimensions.
        vertical_axis: Optional up direction to prevent worlds from being placed below ground level.
            If specified, correction along this axis will be nullified.
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of shape (num_worlds, 3) with computed 3D positions for each world.
    """
    # Handle edge case
    if num_worlds <= 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    
    # Compute positional offsets per world
    cell_size = np.array(cell_size, dtype=np.float32)
    active_axes = np.nonzero(cell_size)[0]
    dim_count = active_axes.shape[0]
    
    if dim_count > 0:
        grid_side = int(np.ceil(num_worlds ** (1.0 / dim_count)))
        positions = []
        
        if dim_count == 1:
            for idx in range(num_worlds):
                positions.append(idx * cell_size)
        elif dim_count == 2:
            for idx in range(num_worlds):
                row = idx // grid_side
                col = idx % grid_side
                pos = np.zeros(3)
                pos[active_axes[0]] = row * cell_size[active_axes[0]]
                pos[active_axes[1]] = col * cell_size[active_axes[1]]
                positions.append(pos)
        elif dim_count == 3:
            for idx in range(num_worlds):
                layer = idx // (grid_side * grid_side)
                row = (idx // grid_side) % grid_side
                col = idx % grid_side
                pos = np.zeros(3)
                pos[0] = layer * cell_size[0]
                pos[1] = row * cell_size[1]
                pos[2] = col * cell_size[2]
                positions.append(pos)
                
        positions = np.array(positions, dtype=np.float32)
    else:
        positions = np.zeros((num_worlds, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    
    # Center the grid
    lower_bound = np.min(positions, axis=0)
    upper_bound = np.max(positions, axis=0)
    center_correction = lower_bound + (upper_bound - lower_bound) / 2.0
    
    # Ensure the worlds are not shifted below the ground plane
    if vertical_axis is not None:
        center_correction[Axis.from_any(vertical_axis)] = 0.0
        
    positions -= center_correction
    return positions

__all__ = [
    "check_conditional_support",
    "clear_git_cache",
    "compute_world_positions",
    "download_asset",
    "load_texture",
    "normalize_texture",
    "topological_sort",
    "topological_sort_undirected",
]

from copy import deepcopy

import mindspeed.megatron_adaptor
import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from megatron.core import mpu
from megatron.core.enums import ModelType
from megatron.training import get_args, print_rank_0
from megatron.training.utils import average_losses_across_data_parallel_group
from mindspeed_mm.configs.config import mm_extra_args_provider
from mindspeed_mm.data import build_mm_dataloader, build_mm_dataset
from mindspeed_mm.data.data_utils.utils import build_iterations
from mindspeed_mm.models.qwen2vl_model import Qwen2VLModel
from mindspeed_mm.training import pretrain
from mindspeed_mm.utils.transformer_model_config import get_model_config
from mindspeed_mm.patchs import dummy_optimizer_patch

def model_provider(pre_process=True, post_process=True):
    """Builds the model."""
    args = get_args()
    print_rank_0("constructing QWen2VL model ...")
    vlm_cfg = deepcopy(args.mm.model)
    # adjust model setup for pipeline parallel execution
    vlm_cfg.pre_process = pre_process
    vlm_cfg.post_process = post_process
    
    if vlm_cfg.image_encoder:
        vlm_cfg.image_encoder.vision_encoder = get_model_config(vlm_cfg.image_encoder.vision_encoder)
        vlm_cfg.image_encoder.vision_projector = get_model_config(vlm_cfg.image_encoder.vision_projector)
        vlm_cfg.text_decoder = get_model_config(vlm_cfg.text_decoder)
        model = Qwen2VLModel(vlm_cfg)
        freeze_vision = getattr(vlm_cfg.image_encoder.vision_encoder, 'freeze', True)
        freeze_proj = getattr(vlm_cfg.image_encoder.vision_projector, 'freeze', True)
        model.freeze(freeze_image_encoder=freeze_vision, freeze_image_projection=freeze_proj)
    else:
        vlm_cfg.text_decoder = get_model_config(vlm_cfg.text_decoder)
        model = Qwen2VLModel(vlm_cfg)
        
    return model

def get_batch(data_iterator):
    """Produce a batch of data."""
    if data_iterator is not None:
        batch = next(data_iterator)
    else:
        raise ValueError("Data iterator is None. Cannot fetch batch.")
    
    device = torch.cuda.current_device()
    input_ids = batch['input_ids'].to(device)
    labels = batch['labels'].to(device)
    attention_mask = batch['attention_mask'].to(device)
    
    has_image = 'pixel_values' in batch and 'image_grid_thw' in batch
    has_video = 'pixel_values_videos' in batch and 'video_grid_thw' in batch
    
    pixel_values = None
    image_grid_thw = None
    
    if has_image or has_video:
        if has_image:
            pixel_values = batch['pixel_values'].to(device)
            image_grid_thw = batch['image_grid_thw'].to(device)
        if has_video:
            pixel_values = batch['pixel_values_videos'].to(device)
            image_grid_thw = batch['video_grid_thw'].to(device)
            
    batch_dict = {
        'input_ids': input_ids,
        'labels': labels,
        'attention_mask': attention_mask,
        'pixel_values': pixel_values,
        'image_grid_thw': image_grid_thw
    }
    
    return (batch_dict['input_ids'], 
            batch_dict['labels'], 
            batch_dict['attention_mask'], 
            batch_dict['pixel_values'], 
            batch_dict['image_grid_thw'])

def loss_func(output_tensor):
    """Compute the loss value."""
    args = get_args()
    loss = output_tensor['loss'].mean()
    metrics = {}
    
    if args.log_tps:
        B, S, _ = output_tensor['logits'].shape
        dp_world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size(group=mpu.get_data_parallel_group())
        tokens_per_sample = torch.tensor(S, device=output_tensor['logits'].device) / dp_world_size
        torch.distributed.all_reduce(tokens_per_sample, group=mpu.get_data_parallel_group())
        metrics["tokens per sample"] = tokens_per_sample
        
    averaged_loss = average_losses_across_data_parallel_group([loss])
    metrics["loss"] = averaged_loss[0]
    loss_clone = loss.unsqueeze(0).clone()
    
    return loss_clone, metrics

def forward_step(data_iterator, model):
    """Execute forward pass."""
    input_ids, labels, attention_mask, pixel_values, image_grid_thw = get_batch(data_iterator)
    output_tensor = model(input_ids=input_ids, 
                         pixel_values=pixel_values, 
                         image_grid_thw=image_grid_thw,
                         attention_mask=attention_mask, 
                         labels=labels)
    return output_tensor, loss_func

def train_valid_test_datasets_provider(train_val_test_num_samples):
    """Create train, validation, and test datasets."""
    args = get_args()
    data_config = args.mm.data
    datasets = build_mm_dataset(data_config.dataset_param)
    
    build_dataloader_fn = partial(build_mm_dataloader,
                                  dataloader_param=data_config.dataloader_param,
                                  process_group=mpu.get_data_parallel_group(),
                                  dataset_param=data_config.dataset_param,
                                  consumed_samples=args.consumed_train_samples)
    
    if isinstance(datasets, tuple) and len(datasets) == 2:
        train_dataset, val_dataset = datasets
        train_loader = build_dataloader_fn(train_dataset)
        valid_loader = build_dataloader_fn(val_dataset)
        train_loader, valid_loader, test_loader = build_iterations(train_loader, valid_loader)
    else:
        train_dataset = datasets
        val_ratio = getattr(data_config.dataset_param.basic_parameters, 'val_rate', 0.0)
        
        if isinstance(train_dataset, Dataset) and val_ratio > 0:
            split_dataset = train_dataset.train_test_split(test_size=val_ratio, seed=args.seed)
            train_dataset, val_dataset = split_dataset['train'], split_dataset['test']
            train_loader = build_dataloader_fn(train_dataset)
            valid_loader = build_dataloader_fn(val_dataset)
            train_loader, valid_loader, test_loader = build_iterations(train_loader, valid_loader)
        else:
            train_loader = build_dataloader_fn(train_dataset)
            train_loader, valid_loader, test_loader = build_iterations(train_loader)
            
    return train_loader, valid_loader, test_loader

if __name__ == "__main__":
    train_valid_test_datasets_provider.is_distributed = True
    pretrain(
        train_valid_test_datasets_provider,
        model_provider,
        ModelType.encoder_or_decoder,
        forward_step,
        extra_args_provider=mm_extra_args_provider,
        args_defaults={"dataloader_type": "external"},
    )

import csv
import os

def prepare_binaural_wsj0mix(
    exp_name,
    data_dir,
    output_dir,
    num_sources=2,
    skip_preparation=False,
    sample_rate=8000,
    dataset_version="min",
):
    """
    Prepares binaural wsj2mix if num_sources=2 and binaural wsj3mix if num_sources=3.
    Arguments:
    ----------
        data_dir (str) : path for the binaural-wsj0mix dataset.
        output_dir (str) : path where we save the csv file.
        num_sources (int): number of speakers
        skip_preparation (bool): If True, skip data preparation
    """
    if skip_preparation:
        return
    if "noise" in exp_name:
        create_binaural_wsj0mix2_noise_csv(data_dir, output_dir, sample_rate, dataset_version)
    elif "reverb" in exp_name:
        create_binaural_wsj0mix2_reverb_csv(data_dir, output_dir, sample_rate, dataset_version)
    elif num_sources == 2:
        create_binaural_wsj0mix2_csv(data_dir, output_dir, sample_rate, dataset_version)
    elif num_sources == 3:
        create_binaural_wsj0mix3_csv(data_dir, output_dir, sample_rate, dataset_version)
    else:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported preparation mode")

def create_binaural_wsj0mix2_csv(
    data_dir,
    output_dir,
    sample_rate,
    dataset_version,
    filename_prefix="binaural_wsj0-2mix_",
    dataset_splits=["tr", "cv", "tt"],
):
    """
    This function creates the csv files to get the speechbrain data loaders for the binaural-wsj0mix2 dataset.
    Arguments:
        data_dir (str) : path for the binaural-wsj0mix dataset.
        output_dir (str) : path where we save the csv file
    """
    if sample_rate == 8000:
        rate_suffix = "8k"
    elif sample_rate == 16000:
        rate_suffix = "16k"
    else:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported sampling rate")
    
    for split in dataset_splits:
        mix_directory = os.path.join(
            data_dir, "wav{}".format(rate_suffix), dataset_version, split, "mix/"
        )
        source1_directory = os.path.join(
            data_dir, "wav{}".format(rate_suffix), dataset_version, split, "s1/"
        )
        source2_directory = os.path.join(
            data_dir, "wav{}".format(rate_suffix), dataset_version, split, "s2/"
        )
        
        audio_files = os.listdir(mix_directory)
        mix_file_paths = [mix_directory + fname for fname in audio_files]
        s1_file_paths = [source1_directory + fname for fname in audio_files]
        s2_file_paths = [source2_directory + fname for fname in audio_files]
        
        header_columns = [
            "ID",
            "duration",
            "mix_wav",
            "mix_wav_format",
            "mix_wav_opts",
            "s1_wav",
            "s1_wav_format",
            "s1_wav_opts",
            "s2_wav",
            "s2_wav_format",
            "s2_wav_opts",
        ]
        
        with open(
            os.path.join(output_dir, filename_prefix + split + ".csv"), "w"
        ) as csv_file:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(csv_file, fieldnames=header_columns)
            writer.writeheader()
            
            for idx, (mix_path, src1_path, src2_path) in enumerate(
                zip(mix_file_paths, s1_file_paths, s2_file_paths)
            ):
                entry = {
                    "ID": idx,
                    "duration": 1.0,
                    "mix_wav": mix_path,
                    "mix_wav_format": "wav",
                    "mix_wav_opts": None,
                    "s1_wav": src1_path,
                    "s1_wav_format": "wav",
                    "s1_wav_opts": None,
                    "s2_wav": src2_path,
                    "s2_wav_format": "wav",
                    "s2_wav_opts": None,

import warnings
from contextlib import contextmanager
from ....processing_utils import ProcessorMixin

class Speech2Text2Processor(ProcessorMixin):
    r"""
    Creates a Speech2Text2 processor that combines a Speech2Text2 feature extractor and tokenizer into one unit.
    [`Speech2Text2Processor`] provides all capabilities of [`AutoFeatureExtractor`] and [`Speech2Text2Tokenizer`].
    Refer to [`~Speech2Text2Processor.__call__`] and [`~Speech2Text2Processor.decode`] for further details.
    Args:
        feature_extractor (`AutoFeatureExtractor`):
            An instance of [`AutoFeatureExtractor`]. This component is mandatory.
        tokenizer (`Speech2Text2Tokenizer`):
            An instance of [`Speech2Text2Tokenizer`]. This component is mandatory.
    """
    feature_extractor_class = "AutoFeatureExtractor"
    tokenizer_class = "Speech2Text2Tokenizer"

    def __init__(self, feature_extractor, tokenizer):
        super().__init__(feature_extractor, tokenizer)
        self.active_processor = self.feature_extractor
        self._inside_target_context = False

    def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """
        In standard usage, this method passes all arguments to AutoFeatureExtractor's
        [`~AutoFeatureExtractor.__call__`] and returns its result. When used inside the
        [`~Speech2Text2Processor.as_target_processor`] context, it instead delegates to
        Speech2Text2Tokenizer's [`~Speech2Text2Tokenizer.__call__`]. See the respective docstrings
        for detailed information.
        """
        # Maintain backward compatibility
        if self._inside_target_context:
            return self.active_processor(*args, **kwargs)

        if "raw_speech" in kwargs:
            warnings.warn("Using `raw_speech` as a keyword argument is deprecated. Use `audio` instead.")
            audio_input = kwargs.pop("raw_speech")
        else:
            audio_input = kwargs.pop("audio", None)

        sample_rate = kwargs.pop("sampling_rate", None)
        input_text = kwargs.pop("text", None)

        if len(args) > 0:
            audio_input = args[0]
            args = args[1:]

        if audio_input is None and input_text is None:
            raise ValueError("You need to specify either an `audio` or `text` input to process.")

        if audio_input is not None:
            features = self.feature_extractor(audio_input, *args, sampling_rate=sample_rate, **kwargs)

        if input_text is not None:
            encoded = self.tokenizer(input_text, **kwargs)

        if input_text is None:
            return features
        elif audio_input is None:
            return encoded
        else:
            features["labels"] = encoded["input_ids"]
            return features

    def batch_decode(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """
        Forwards all arguments to Speech2Text2Tokenizer's [`~PreTrainedTokenizer.batch_decode`].
        Please consult the corresponding docstring for more details.
        """
        return self.tokenizer.batch_decode(*args, **kwargs)

    def decode(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """
        Forwards all arguments to Speech2Text2Tokenizer's [`~PreTrainedTokenizer.decode`].
        Please consult the corresponding docstring for more details.
        """
        return self.tokenizer.decode(*args, **kwargs)

    @contextmanager
    def as_target_processor(self):
        """
        Temporarily switches to using the tokenizer for processing inputs. Useful during fine-tuning
        of Speech2Text2 when encoding labels.
        """
        warnings.warn(
            "`as_target_processor` is deprecated and will be removed in v5 of Transformers. You can process your "
            "labels by using the argument `text` of the regular `__call__` method (either in the same call as "
            "your audio inputs, or in a separate call."
        )
        self._inside_target_context = True
        self.active_processor = self.tokenizer
        yield
        self.active_processor = self.feature_extractor
        self._inside_target_context = False

def test_emit_event_executes_without_exception(behavior_runner):
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": "sample_event"})

def test_emit_event_initializes_new_event_if_missing(behavior_runner):
    assert "fresh_ev" not in behavior_runner._events
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": "fresh_ev"})
    with behavior_runner._events_lock:
        assert "fresh_ev" in behavior_runner._events

def test_emit_event_sets_newly_created_event(behavior_runner):
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": "brand_new_event"})
    with behavior_runner._events_lock:
        assert behavior_runner._events["brand_new_event"].is_set()

def test_emit_event_reactivates_existing_event(behavior_runner):
    active_flag = threading.Event()
    behavior_runner._events["prev_event"] = active_flag
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": "prev_event"})
    assert active_flag.is_set()

def test_emit_event_restores_cleared_event_state(behavior_runner):
    """emit_event should re-activate an event even after it was cleared."""
    flag = threading.Event()
    flag.set()
    flag.clear()
    assert not flag.is_set()
    behavior_runner._events["cleared_flag"] = flag
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": "cleared_flag"})
    assert flag.is_set()

def test_emit_event_retains_original_event_instance(behavior_runner):
    """emit_event must preserve the original Event object instead of replacing it."""
    original_flag = threading.Event()
    behavior_runner._events["kept_flag"] = original_flag
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": "kept_flag"})
    with behavior_runner._events_lock:
        assert behavior_runner._events["kept_flag"] is original_flag

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_emit_event_ignores_missing_event_key(behavior_runner):
    """If 'event' key is absent, no changes should occur and no exception raised."""
    initial_keys = set(behavior_runner._events.keys())
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({})
    final_keys = set(behavior_runner._events.keys())
    assert initial_keys == final_keys

def test_emit_event_handles_empty_string_event_key(behavior_runner):
    """An empty string for 'event' should be handled gracefully."""
    behavior_runner._step_emit_event({"event": ""})

    """emit_event should release a concurrent wait_for_event call."""
    outcomes = []

        behavior_runner._step_wait_for_event({"event": "concurrent_ev", "timeout_s": 3.0, "clear_after": False})

import wave
from machine import I2S
import _thread

I2SDataPin = 9
I2SBitClockPin = 10
I2SChannelPin = 11
AudioBlockSize = 1024
CSVAsciiBlockSize = 512

class WavePlayer:
    def __init__(self, wavefilename, csvfilename=None, binblocksize=0, verbose=0):
        self.verbose = verbose
        self.filename = wavefilename
        try:
            self.file = wave.open(self.filename)
        except:
            self.file = None
            return
        
        self._volume = 0.5
        # Open the csvfile if specified
        self.fullqueue = []
        self.emptyqueue = []
        self.queuesize = 0
        self.binblocksize = 0
        self.csvfile = None
        
        # Set up for binary or ascii control file I/O
        if binblocksize > 0:
            # Use binary file format with fixed size records
            try:
                self.csvfile = open(csvfilename, 'rb')
                # If opening is successful, set up data queue
                self.binblocksize = binblocksize
                # Create a semaphore lock for threads to coordinate getting and putting data in queue
                self.queuelock = _thread.allocate_lock()
                # Fill the queue initially
                self.queuesize = 5
                # initially fill the empty queue
                for i in range(self.queuesize):
                    self.emptyqueue.append(bytearray(binblocksize))
                # Read in the first two blocks of binary data
                self.bfillqueue()
            except:
                pass    # Ignore any errors including filename is None
        else:
            # Use ASCII file format with variable size records
            try:
                self.csvfile = open(csvfilename, 'r')
                # If opening is successful, set up data queue
                # Create a semaphore lock for threads to coordinate getting and putting data in queue
                self.queuelock = _thread.allocate_lock()
                # Fill the queue initially
                self.queuesize = 5
                # initially fill the queue
                self.fillqueue()
            except:
                pass    # Ignore any errors including filename is None
        
        # Set up ping-pong audio buffers
        self.audiodata = [None] * 2
        self.currbuffer = 0
        self.audiodata[0] = bytearray(AudioBlockSize)
        self.audiodata[1] = bytearray(AudioBlockSize)
        
        # Initialize stats
        self.startTicks = 0
        self.sumuploadticks = 0
        self.sumreadfilemsec = 0
        self.suspendedusec = 0
        self.blocksplayed = 0
        self.csvfiletime = 0
        
        # Compute number of frames in a 512-byte block
        self.blockframes = int(512/self.file.getsampwidth()/self.file.getnchannels())
        
        # Stop Flag set to not play initially
        self.stopflag = True
        self.controlstop = True
        
        # Set semaphore to indicate that we need to write again
        self.emptyflag = True
        
        # Set up pins for I2S
        datapin = Pin(I2SDataPin, Pin.OUT)
        bitclockpin = Pin(I2SBitClockPin, Pin.OUT)
        channelpin = Pin(I2SChannelPin, Pin.OUT)
        
        # Create the audio out channel over I2S
        self.audio_out = I2S(1,
                sck=bitclockpin, ws=channelpin, sd=datapin,
                mode=I2S.TX,
                bits=self.file.getsampwidth() * 8,
                format=(I2S.MONO if self.file.getnchannels() == 1 else I2S.STEREO),
                rate=self.file.getframerate(),
                ibuf=AudioBlockSize*4)
        
        # Create a semaphore lock for outside reads to avoid interfering with reads in this thread
        self.readLock = _thread.allocate_lock()
        
        # Read in first buffer so we are ready to play
        self.loadbuffer(self.currbuffer)
        self.stopflag = False
        if self.csvfile is not None: self.controlstop = False
    
    def fillqueue(self):
        startTicks = utime.ticks_us()
        while len(self.fullqueue) < self.queuesize:
            line = self.csvfile.readline()
            self.queuelock.acquire()
            self.fullqueue.append(line)
            self.queuelock.release()
        self.csvfiletime += utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), startTicks)
    
    def bfillqueue(self):
        startTicks = utime.ticks_us()
        while len(self.emptyqueue) > 0:
            # Pop empty buffer off of empty queue
            self.queuelock.acquire()
            buffer = self.emptyqueue.pop(0)
            self.queuelock.release()
            # Fill it up
            BLOCKSIZE = 512  # Don't read more than 512 bytes per read
            f = self.csvfile
            n = self.binblocksize
            mv = memoryview(buffer)
            bytes_read = 0
            for i in range(0, n - BLOCKSIZE, BLOCKSIZE):
                bytes_read += f.readinto(mv[i:i + BLOCKSIZE])
            if bytes_read < n:
                bytes_read += f.readinto(mv[bytes_read:n])
            # Push it onto full queue
            if bytes_read == 0: buffer = b''    # Klugey way to tell it the file is empty so it will stop??
            self.queuelock.acquire()
            self.fullqueue.append(buffer)
            self.queuelock.release()
        self.csvfiletime += utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), startTicks)
    
    def readline(self, emptybuf=None):
        # Must be called from another thread to prevent locking
        if self.controlstop:
            return('')
        if emptybuf is not None and self.binblocksize > 0:
            self.emptyqueue.append(emptybuf)
        while len(self.fullqueue) < 1:
            self.suspendedusec += 20
            utime.sleep_us(20)
        self.queuelock.acquire()
        outline = self.fullqueue.pop(0)
        self.queuelock.release()
        self.controlstop = len(outline) == 0
        return outline
    
    def close(self):
        # Just to make it look like a file
        self.stop()
        pass
    
    def irq(self, arg):
        self.emptyflag = True
        if self.verbose > 1: print('In irq arg:', arg)
    
    def play(self):
        if self.file is None: return
        if self.verbose > 0: print('Running play() in thread', _thread.get_ident())
        # Play until done or stopped
        self.stopflag = False
        if self.csvfile is not None: self.controlstop = False
        # Kick off playback in a new thread
        _thread.start_new_thread(self.threadplay, (False,))
    
    def threadplay(self, dummy):
        if self.verbose > 0: print('Running threadplay() in thread', _thread.get_ident())
        # Initialize statistics
        self.startTicks = utime.ticks_us()
        self.sumuploadticks = 0
        self.sumreadfileticks = 0
        self.suspendedusec = 0
        self.blocksplayed = 0
        self.csvfiletime = 0
        
        # Set interrupt service routine to make write non-blocking
        self.audio_out.irq(self.irq)
        
        # Play until end of data or stopped
        while not self.stopflag or not self.controlstop: 
            self.playblock(False)
        
        # Try to more explicitly kill the thread
        _thread.exit()
    
    def playblock(self, junk):
        #print('Entered playblock')
        # Make sure data queue is full
        if not self.controlstop:
            if self.binblocksize > 0:
                self.bfillqueue()
            else:
                self.fillqueue()
        
        # Check to see if we are stopped
        if not self.stopflag:
            #if self.verbose > 1: print('Running playblock() in thread', _thread.get_ident())
            if self.emptyflag:
                self.emptyflag = False
                # Play one block of audio data from current ping-pong buffer
                startTicks = utime.ticks_us()
                self.audio_out.write(self.audiodata[self.currbuffer])
                totaluploadticks = utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), startTicks)
                if self.verbose > 1: print('Ticks to write block to i2s', totaluploadticks)
                self.sumuploadticks += totaluploadticks
                self.blocksplayed += 1
    
                # Fill the buffer while playing previous buffer
                # Switch to other buffer
                self.currbuffer = 1 - self.currbuffer
                startTicks = utime.ticks_us()
                self.loadbuffer(self.currbuffer)
                self.sumreadfileticks += utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), startTicks)
    
    def loadbuffer(self, buffer):
        startTicks = utime.ticks_us()
        self.readLock.acquire()
        size = self.file.readframes(AudioBlockSize, databuf=self.audiodata[buffer])
        if size == 0: self.stopflag = True
        self.readLock.release()
        if self.verbose > 1: print('Ticks to read block:', utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), startTicks), 'usec')
    
    def stop(self):
        # Stop playing
        self.stopflag = True
        self.controlstop = True
        # Dump statistics
        if self.verbose > 0:
            print('----------------------------------------------------')
            print('    Audio Thread Statistics')
            print('Total time spent reading control file:', self.csvfiletime, 'usec')
            print('Total time spent reading audio data  :', self.sumreadfileticks, 'usec')
            print('Total time spent uploading data      :', self.sumuploadticks, 'usec')
            print('Total estimated time queue waiting   :', self.suspendedusec, 'usec')
            print('Total time                           :', utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), self.startTicks)/1000000, 'sec')
            print('Total audio played                   :', self.blocksplayed * self.blockframes * AudioBlockSize / 512 / self.file.getframerate(), 'sec')
            print('----------------------------------------------------')
        pass
    
    def rewind(self):
        if self.file is None: return
        if not self.stopflag or not self.controlstop: self.stop()
        # Get ready to start from the top
        self.file.close()
        try:
            self.file = wave.open(self.filename)
        except:
            self.file = None
    
    def volume(self, newVolume=None):
        if newVolume is None:
            return self._volume
        else:
            self._volume = newVolume
    
    def playing(self):
        return not self.stopflag or not self.controlstop

import machine
import os
import sdcard

def mountSDCard(mountpoint='/sd'):
    # Assign chip select (CS) pin (and start it high)
    cs = machine.Pin(17, machine.Pin.OUT)
    # Initialize SPI peripheral (start with 1 MHz)
    spi = machine.SPI(0,
                      baudrate=4000000,
                      polarity=0,
                      phase=0,
                      bits=8,
                      firstbit=machine.SPI.MSB,
                      sck=machine.Pin(18, machine.Pin.OUT),
                      mosi=machine.Pin(19, machine.Pin.OUT),
                      miso=machine.Pin(16, machine.Pin.OUT))
    # Initialize SD card
    sd = sdcard.SDCard(spi, cs)
    # Set the speed to fast enough for audio
    # Have to set it here because the SDCard constructor above sets the baudrate back to 1,000,000
    spi.init(baudrate=40000000)
    # Mount filesystem
    vfs = os.VfsFat(sd)
    os.mount(vfs, mountpoint)

import select
import sys

# Create object for communicating over USB
inpoll = select.poll()
inpoll.register(sys.stdin.buffer, select.POLLIN)

def isThereInput():
    result = inpoll.poll(0)
    return len(result) > 0

def handleInput():
    inline = sys.stdin.buffer.readline().decode('utf-8')
    if len(inline) > 6 and inline[0:6] == 'status':
        # Handle status request
        if inline[6] == 'b':
            # Wants block sizes
            blockSizes = tables.getBinarysizes()
            print(tables.PreferBinary)
            print(blockSizes[0], blockSizes[1], blockSizes[2], blockSizes[3])
    elif inline[0] == 'a':
        # Trigger one playback
        return 1
    elif inline[0] == 'x':
        # Wait 2 seconds for commlib to close connection
        utime.sleep_ms(2000)
        # Restart everything
        machine.reset()
    elif inline[0] == 'd':
        # Set an individual digital port
        try:
            vals = inline.split()
            channel = int(vals[1]) # - MaxTotalServos # Move down
            value = int(vals[2])
            setDigital(channel, value, show=True)
        except:
            pass
    elif inline[0] == 's':
        # Set an individual servo
        try:
            vals = inline.split()
            channel = int(vals[1])
            value = int(vals[2])
            setServo(channel, value, push=True)
        except:
            pass
    elif inline[0] == 'b':
        # Upload entire binary file
        try:
            vals = inline.split()
            filename = vals[1]
            fsize = int(vals[2])
            file = open(filename, 'wb')
            line = sys.stdin.buffer.read(min(fsize, 512))
            while fsize > 0:
                bwritten = file.write(binascii.unhexlify(line))
                fsize -= len(line)
                if fsize > 0: line = sys.stdin.buffer.read(min(fsize, 512))
            file.close()
            if tables.PreferBinary:
                # Convert the file to binary format
                tables.csvToBin(filename)
            # Wait 2 seconds for commlib to close connection
            utime.sleep_ms(2000)
            machine.reset() # Reboot to get new files into playback list?
        except:
            # sys.stderr.write('\nWhoops - Unable to write file %d\n' % filename)
            pass
    elif inline[0] == 'c':
        try:
            vals = inline.split()
            filename = vals[1]
            checksum = filecrc16(filename)
            print(checksum)
        except:
            print(-1)
    return 0

################################### File Utilities ############################
def filecrc16(fname):
    # Computes and returns a 16-bit Cyclic Redundancy Checksum of the specified file
    PRESET = 0xFFFF
    POLYNOMIAL = 0xA001 # bit reverse of 0x8005
    try:
        crc = PRESET
        file = open(fname, 'rb')
        data = file.read(256)
        while len(data) > 0:
            for c in data:
                crc = crc ^ c
                for j in range(8):
                    if crc & 0x01:
                        crc = (crc >> 1) ^ POLYNOMIAL
                    else:
                        crc = crc >> 1
            data = file.read(256)
        file.close()
        return crc
    except:
        return -1

def isfile(testfile):
    try:
        size = os.stat(testfile)[6]
        return size > 0
    except:
        return False

def pathjoin(path, fname):
    if path is not None:
        if path[-1] != '/':
            path += '/'
        fname = path + fname
    return fname

def findAnimFiles(dir='/anims'):
    # Find animation files
    # Create empty list of csv/audio file pairs
    animList = []
    idler = None
    
    # Look for binary or ascii files?
    if tables.PreferBinary:
        ext = '.bin'
    else:
        ext = '.csv'
    
    # Check for an existing list of files
    testfile = pathjoin(dir, 'animlist')
    if isfile(testfile):
        with open(testfile, 'r') as infile:
            line = infile.readline()
            while len(line) > 0:
                names = line.split()
                if len(names) == 2:
                    # Should be both a csv filename and an audio filename
                    # Not checking for existence yet
                    animList.append(names)
                elif len(names) == 1:
                    # Should be a fileroot that will be appended with .csv or .bin or .wav
                    tpair = []
                    if isfile(names[0] + ext):
                        tpair.append(names[0] + ext)
                    elif isfile(pathjoin(dir, names[0] + ext)):
                        tpair.append(pathjoin(dir, names[0] + ext))
                    else:
                        tpair.append(None)
                    if isfile(names[0] + '.wav'):
                        tpair.append(names[0] + '.wav')
                    elif isfile(pathjoin(dir, names[0] + '.wav')):
                        tpair.append(pathjoin(dir, names[0] + '.wav'))
                    else:
                        tpair.append(None)
                    animList.append(tpair)
                elif len(names) == 3 and names[2] == 'idle':
                    idler = names[0:2]
                line = infile.readline()
    else:
        # Check for matching filename pairs
        try:
            filelist = os.listdir(dir)
            for filename in filelist:
                tpair = []
                if filename[-4:] == ext:
                    tpair.append(pathjoin(dir, filename))
                    tname = filename[:-4] + '.wav'
                    if tname in filelist:
                        tpair.append(pathjoin(dir, tname))
                        if tname == 'idle.wav':
                            idler = tpair
                        else:
                            animList.append(tpair)
        except:
            # Ignore problems
            pass
    return animList,idler

# GH#310: PATTERN/REGEX values must always be quoted in emission.
from octave_mcp.core.ast_nodes import Assignment
from octave_mcp.core.emitter import emit, emit_assignment
from octave_mcp.core.parser import parse, parse_with_warnings

class TestPatternRegexQuotePreservation:
    """GH#310: PATTERN/REGEX values must always be quoted in emission."""
    def test_pattern_single_word_preserves_quotes(self):
        """PATTERN::"Workaround" must round-trip as PATTERN::"Workaround", not bare."""
        input_text = '===TEST===\nGRAMMAR:\n  PATTERN::"Workaround"\n===END===\n'
        document = parse(input_text)
        output = emit(document)
        assert 'PATTERN::"Workaround"' in output
    
    def test_pattern_multi_word_preserves_quotes(self):
        """PATTERN::"Quick fix src/App.tsx" preserves quotes (multi-word)."""
        input_text = '===TEST===\nGRAMMAR:\n  PATTERN::"Quick fix src/App.tsx"\n===END===\n'
        document = parse(input_text)
        output = emit(document)
        assert 'PATTERN::"Quick fix src/App.tsx"' in output
    
    def test_regex_special_chars_preserves_quotes(self):
        """REGEX::"^\\[SYSTEM_STATE\\]" preserves quotes (special chars)."""
        input_text = '===TEST===\nGRAMMAR:\n  REGEX::"^\\\\[SYSTEM_STATE\\\\]"\n===END===\n'
        document = parse(input_text)
        output = emit(document)
        assert "REGEX::" in output
        # Must be quoted
        regex_line = [line for line in output.split("\n") if "REGEX::" in line][0]
        regex_value = regex_line.split("REGEX::")[1].strip()
        assert regex_value.startswith('"') and regex_value.endswith('"')
    
    def test_pattern_bare_input_gets_auto_quoted(self):
        """PATTERN::Workaround (bare input) must be auto-quoted to PATTERN::"Workaround"."""
        input_text = "===TEST===\nGRAMMAR:\n  PATTERN::Workaround\n===END===\n"
        document = parse(input_text)
        output = emit(document)
        assert 'PATTERN::"Workaround"' in output
    
    def test_non_pattern_key_stays_bare(self):
        """STATUS::active stays bare - only PATTERN/REGEX keys force quotes."""
        input_text = "===TEST===\nSTATUS::active\n===END===\n"
        document = parse(input_text)
        output = emit(document)
        assert "STATUS::active" in output
        assert 'STATUS::"active"' not in output
    
    def test_idempotency_pattern_quoted(self):
        """Normalizing PATTERN::"Workaround" twice produces same output."""
        input_text = '===TEST===\nGRAMMAR:\n  PATTERN::"Workaround"\n===END===\n'
        doc1 = parse(input_text)
        emitted1 = emit(doc1)
        doc2 = parse(emitted1)
        emitted2 = emit(doc2)
        assert emitted1 == emitted2
    
    def test_idempotency_pattern_bare(self):
        """Normalizing bare PATTERN::Workaround twice produces same output."""
        input_text = "===TEST===\nGRAMMAR:\n  PATTERN::Workaround\n===END===\n"
        doc1 = parse(input_text)
        emitted1 = emit(doc1)
        doc2 = parse(emitted1)
        emitted2 = emit(doc2)
        assert emitted1 == emitted2
    
    def test_regex_in_list_preserves_quotes(self):
        """REGEX values inside MUST_USE list preserve quotes."""
        input_text = "===TEST===\n" "GRAMMAR:\n" "  MUST_USE:\n" '    REGEX::"^\\\\[ANALYSIS\\\\]"\n' "===END===\n"
        document = parse(input_text)
        output = emit(document)

# Modified version of the pipeline visualization script
import argparse
import json
import os
from enum import Enum

import matplotlib

class PipelineColor(str, Enum):
    blue_1 = "#305496"
    blue_2 = "#B4C6E7"
    blue_3 = "royalblue"
    blue_4 = "lavender"
    green_1 = "#A9D08E"
    green_2 = "#375623"
    green_3 = "mintcream"
    green_4 = "seagreen"
    yellow_1 = "#d88c2b"
    yellow_2 = "#f6eab4"
    yellow_3 = "#d46014"
    yellow_4 = "#d44014"
    background = "#818181"


def retrieve_color_configuration(vp_size):
    color_config = {
        "forward_fill": [
            PipelineColor.blue_1,
            PipelineColor.blue_2,
            PipelineColor.blue_3,
            PipelineColor.blue_4,
        ],
        "backward_fill": [
            PipelineColor.green_1,
            PipelineColor.green_2,
            PipelineColor.green_3,
            PipelineColor.green_4,
        ],
        "wgrad_fill": [
            PipelineColor.yellow_1,
            PipelineColor.yellow_2,
            PipelineColor.yellow_3,
            PipelineColor.yellow_4,
        ],
        "forward_text": [
            "white",
            "black",
            "white",
            "black",
        ],
        "backward_text": [
            "black",
            "white",
            "black",
            "white",
        ],
        "wgrad_text": [
            "gray",
            "black",
            "gray",
            "black",
        ],
    }

    for _ in range(4, vp_size):
        color_config["forward_fill"].append(
            np.random.rand(
                3,
            )
        )
        color_config["backward_fill"].append(
            np.random.rand(
                3,
            )
        )
        color_config["wgrad_fill"].append(
            np.random.rand(
                3,
            )
        )
        color_config["forward_text"].append("white")
        color_config["backward_text"].append("white")
        color_config["wgrad_text"].append("white")

    return color_config


def compute_bubble_percentage(data, iteration_time, vp_size, num_mbs):
    active_time = 0
    for i in range(vp_size * num_mbs):
        active_time += data["fwd_end"][i] - data["fwd_start"][i]
        active_time += data["bwd_end"][i] - data["bwd_start"][i]
        if "wgrad_start" in data and len(data["wgrad_start"]) > 0:
            active_time += data["wgrad_end"][i] - data["wgrad_start"][i]

    bubble_percentage = (iteration_time - active_time) / iteration_time * 100
    return bubble_percentage


def extract_task_information(task_list):
    task_info_list = []

    for task in task_list:
        task_info = {
            "label": task["title"],
            "iteration_count": len(task["iter_to_vis"]),
            "iterations": task["iter_to_vis"],
        }

        config_file = os.path.join(task["log_path"], "config.json")
        with open(config_file) as f:
            task_info["settings"] = json.load(f)

        pp_size = task_info["settings"]["pp_size"]

        if "vp_size" not in task_info["settings"]:
            task_info["settings"]["vp_size"] = task_info["settings"]["vpp_size"]
        if "num_mbs" not in task_info["settings"]:
            task_info["settings"]["num_mbs"] = task_info["settings"]["micro_batches"]

        vp_size = task_info["settings"]["vp_size"]
        num_mbs = task_info["settings"]["num_mbs"]

        pp_rank_data = {}
        for pp_rank in range(pp_size):
            file_path = os.path.join(task["log_path"], f"pp_rank_{pp_rank}.json")
            with open(file_path) as f:
                pp_rank_data[pp_rank] = json.load(f)

        iteration_data = {}
        max_iteration_time = 0
        for iter_idx in task_info["iterations"]:
            iteration_data[iter_idx] = {}
            iteration_time = pp_rank_data[0][str(iter_idx)]["total"]
            iteration_data[iter_idx]["duration"] = iteration_time
            max_iteration_time = max(iteration_time, max_iteration_time)
            for pp_rank in range(pp_size):
                iteration_data[iter_idx][pp_rank] = pp_rank_data[pp_rank][str(iter_idx)]
                bubble_pct = compute_bubble_percentage(iteration_data[iter_idx][pp_rank], iteration_time, vp_size, num_mbs)
                iteration_data[iter_idx][pp_rank]["bubble"] = bubble_pct

        task_info["iteration_details"] = iteration_data
        task_info["max_duration"] = max_iteration_time

        color_config = retrieve_color_configuration(vp_size)
        task_info["color_config"] = color_config

        task_info_list.append(task_info)

    return task_info_list


def render_block(ax, label, x, y, width, height, text_color, fill_color, border_color, font_size, ha, va):
    block = patches.Rectangle((x, y), width, height, linewidth=0.4, edgecolor=border_color, facecolor=fill_color)
    ax.add_patch(block)
    rx, ry = block.get_xy()
    cx = rx + block.get_width() / 2.0
    cy = ry + block.get_height() / 2.0
    ax.annotate(label, (cx, cy), color=text_color, fontsize=font_size, ha=ha, va=va)


def render_pipeline(ax, iter_info, pp_size, vp_size, num_mbs, chunk_details, color_config, include_wgrad=False):
    phases = ["fwd", "bwd"]
    if include_wgrad:
        phases += ["wgrad"]
    for pp_rank in range(pp_size):
        for phase in phases:
            start_times = iter_info[pp_rank][phase + "_start"]
            end_times = iter_info[pp_rank][phase + "_end"]

            # Update chunk IDs and colors based on minibatch and chunk info
            mb_key = phase + "_minibatch"
            if mb_key in iter_info[pp_rank] and len(iter_info[pp_rank][mb_key]) > 0:
                for i in range(len(iter_info[pp_rank][mb_key])):
                    chunk_details[i]["id"] = iter_info[pp_rank][mb_key][i]

            chunk_id_key = phase + "_chunk"
            if chunk_id_key in iter_info[pp_rank] and len(iter_info[pp_rank][chunk_id_key]) > 0:
                for i in range(len(iter_info[pp_rank][chunk_id_key])):
                    chunk_id = iter_info[pp_rank][chunk_id_key][i]
                    chunk_details[i][phase + "_fill"] = color_config[phase + "_fill"][chunk_id]
                    chunk_details[i][phase + "_text"] = color_config[phase + "_text"][chunk_id]

            for i in range(vp_size * num_mbs):
                mbs_id = chunk_details[i]["id"]
                x = start_times[i]
                y = pp_size - pp_rank - 1
                w = end_times[i] - start_times[i]
                h = 1
                fill_color = chunk_details[i][phase + "_fill"]
                text_color = chunk_details[i][phase + "_text"]

                font_size = 3

                render_block(
                    ax, mbs_id, x, y, w, h, text_color, fill_color, "black", font_size, "center", "center"
                )

        bubble = iter_info[pp_rank]["bubble"]
        memory = iter_info[pp_rank]["memory"]
        text = f"(Bubble: {bubble:.2f}%)\n(Mem: {memory:.2f} GB)"

        render_block(ax, text, x + w, y, 10, h, "white", "none", "none", 5, "left", "center")


def prepare_chunk_details(num_mbs, pp_size, vp_size, color_config):
    chunk_details = []
    id_sequence = [i + 1 for i in range(num_mbs)]
    color_index_sequence = [0 for _ in range(num_mbs)]
    chunk_count = num_mbs // pp_size
    if vp_size > 1:
        color_index_sequence = [[i] * pp_size for i in range(vp_size)] * chunk_count
        color_index_sequence = sum(color_index_sequence, [])
        id_sequence_split = [id_sequence[i : i + pp_size] for i in range(0, len(id_sequence), pp_size)]
        temp_id_sequence = id_sequence_split.copy()
        for i in range(chunk_count, 0, -1):
            temp_id_sequence.insert(i, id_sequence_split[i - 1] * (vp_size - 1))
        id_sequence = sum(temp_id_sequence, [])
        id_sequence = sum(temp_id_sequence, [])

    for i in range(num_mbs * vp_size):
        color_idx = color_index_sequence[i]
        chunk_details.append(
            {
                "id": id_sequence[i],
                "fwd_fill": color_config["forward_fill"][color_idx],
                "bwd_fill": color_config["backward_fill"][color_idx],
                "wgrad_fill": color_config["wgrad_fill"][color_idx],
                "fwd_text": color_config["forward_text"][color_idx],
                "bwd_text": color_config["backward_text"][color_idx],
                "wgrad_text": color_config["wgrad_text"][color_idx],
            }
        )
    return chunk_details


def render_subplots(axs, task_info, max_iteration_time):
    color_config = task_info["color_config"]
    pp_size = task_info["settings"]["pp_size"]
    vp_size = task_info["settings"]["vp_size"]
    num_mbs = task_info["settings"]["num_mbs"]

    chunk_details = prepare_chunk_details(num_mbs, pp_size, vp_size, color_config)

    for ax_idx, iter_idx in enumerate(task_info["iterations"]):
        ax = axs.flat[ax_idx] if type(axs) == np.ndarray else axs
        iter_data = task_info["iteration_details"][iter_idx]
        max_memory = max(iter_data[i]["memory"] for i in range(pp_size))
        iteration_time = iter_data["duration"]
        sub_title = f"iteration {iter_idx} (duration: {iteration_time:.0f}ms, max_mem: {max_memory:.2f}GB)"
        ax.set_title(sub_title, fontsize="small")
        ax.set_xlim((0, max_iteration_time * 1.1))
        ax.set_ylim((0, pp_size))
        ax.set_xlabel("time(ms)", loc="right")
        ax.set_facecolor(PipelineColor.background)

        yaxis_labels = [f"PP-{i}" for i in range(pp_size - 1, -1, -1)]
        y_positions = np.arange(len(yaxis_labels)) + 0.5
        ax.set_yticks(y_positions, labels=yaxis_labels)

        legend_elements = []

        include_wgrad = "wgrad_start" in iter_data[0] and len(iter_data[0]["wgrad_start"]) > 0

        for i in range(vp_size):
            fwd_block = patches.Patch(
                color=color_config["forward_fill"][i], label="fwd" if vp_size == 1 else "fwd_vpp_" + str(i)
            )
            bwd_block = patches.Patch(
                color=color_config["backward_fill"][i], label="bwd" if vp_size == 1 else "bwd_vpp_" + str(i)
            )
            legend_elements.append(fwd_block)
            legend_elements.append(bwd_block)
            if include_wgrad:
                wgrad_block = patches.Patch(
                    color=color_config["wgrad_fill"][i],
                    label="wgrad" if vp_size == 1 else "wgrad_vpp_" + str(i),
                )
                legend_elements.append(wgrad_block)

        ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, fontsize="6", loc="lower right")

        render_pipeline(ax, iter_data, pp_size, vp_size, num_mbs, chunk_details, color_config, include_wgrad)


def render(task_info_list):
    task_count = len(task_info_list)
    total_iterations = sum(task_info_list[i]["iteration_count"] for i in range(task_count))

    timeline_width = 12
    timeline_height = 3
    fig = plt.figure(
        constrained_layout=True, figsize=(timeline_width, total_iterations * timeline_height), dpi=300
    )
    subfigures = fig.subfigures(task_count, 1)
    max_iteration_time = max(task_info["max_duration"] for task_info in task_info_list)

    for task_idx in range(task_count):
        subfig = subfigures.flat[task_idx] if type(subfigures) == np.ndarray else subfigures
        task_info = task_info_list[task_idx]
        subfig.suptitle(task_info["label"], fontweight="bold")
        axs = subfig.subplots(task_info["iteration_count"], 1)
        render_subplots(axs, task_info, max_iteration_time)

    plt.show()


def render_from_tasks():
    experiments = ["pp8", "pp8_vpp2"]
    task_list = [
        {
            "title": exp,
            "iter_to_vis": [i for i in range(7, 8)],

        }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
