import machine
import utime
import os
import sys
import random
import helpers
import gc
# Constants for port types
DIGITAL = 1
PWM = 2
# Constants for control data file format
CSV = 5
HEX = 6     # No longer used
BIN = 7
firstTime = True    # Flag to prevent idle animation running until started
verbose=False
                # Analysis of memory usage severely affects timing data so keep that in mind
memuse = 0      # 0 = no memory usage stats, 1 = garbage collection count, 2 = debug memuse printing
# LED specifications
# Use the on board LED for status
led_onboard = machine.Pin(25, machine.Pin.OUT)
# Use the off board LED for status too
led_offboard = machine.Pin(26, machine.Pin.OUT)
# Button specifications
# Pin 24 is the onboard USR button on some Pico clones - Do Not Use
# Pin 27 is the opto-isolated Trigger 2 for external stimuli
trigger2 = machine.Pin(27, machine.Pin.IN, machine.Pin.PULL_UP)
trigger2_laststate = True   # True indicates NOT pressed
def opto_button_pressed():
    global trigger2_laststate
    if trigger2.value() != trigger2_laststate:
        utime.sleep_ms(50)    # Debounce switch
        if trigger2.value() != trigger2_laststate:
            trigger2_laststate = trigger2.value()
    return not trigger2_laststate
# Pin 28 is the Trigger 1 button connected to external jumper connector
trigger1 = machine.Pin(28, machine.Pin.IN, machine.Pin.PULL_UP)
trigger1_laststate = True   # True indicates NOT pressed
def button_pressed():
    global trigger1_laststate
    if trigger1.value() != trigger1_laststate:
        utime.sleep_ms(50)    # Debounce switch
        if trigger1.value() != trigger1_laststate:
            trigger1_laststate = trigger1.value()
    return not trigger1_laststate
def toggle_LEDs():
    led_onboard.toggle()
    led_offboard.toggle()
def on_LEDs():
    led_onboard.on()
    led_offboard.on()
def run_animation_sequence(animList, idleanimation=None, randomize=False, continuous=False, skip=False, doOnce=False):
    global firstTime
    helpers.clearAllDigital()   # All digital channels off
    helpers.releaseAllServos()  # All servos relaxed
    # Don't bother with anything if list of animations is empty
    playIndex = 0
    msecPerBlink = 1000    # We will flash at 0.5Hz if we have animations available and 5 Hz if not
    if len(animList) > 0:
        if randomize: playIndex = random.randint(0, len(animList)-1)
    else:
        msecPerBlink = 100
    if verbose: print(animList)
    # Swallow strange initially pressed state
    while button_pressed() or opto_button_pressed():
        utime.sleep_ms(100)
    # Turn off all our status LEDs so they are always synced
    led_onboard.off()
    led_offboard.off()
    # if skip is True then immediately begin execution
    # if continuous is True then execute continuously until interrupted
    # Else Blink at 0.5Hz until button is pressed
    while True:
        # Toggle LED every second until button pressed
        if not continuous and not skip:
            while not button_pressed() and not opto_button_pressed():
                if idleanimation is not None and not firstTime:
                    play_one_anim(idleanimation[0], idleanimation[1], idle=True)
                code = 0
                toggle_LEDs()
                for i in range(msecPerBlink):
                    if helpers.isThereInput():
                        code = helpers.handleInput()
                        if code == 1: break
                    else:
                        utime.sleep_ms(1)
                    if button_pressed():
                        break
                    if opto_button_pressed():
                        break
                if code == 1: break
            # Wait up to 5 seconds for button to be released
            on_LEDs()
            for i in range(100):
                utime.sleep_ms(50)
                if not button_pressed():
                    break
        # If button is STILL pressed, go into continuous loop mode
        if button_pressed():
            # Blink LED at 10 Hz until button released
            while True:
                toggle_LEDs()
                utime.sleep_ms(100)
                if not button_pressed():
                    break
            continuous = True
        if playIndex < len(animList):
            firstTime = False
            # Get next animation to play
            if verbose: print('Print playing animation:', playIndex,'named:',animList[playIndex][0])
            # Play it
            play_one_anim(animList[playIndex][0], animList[playIndex][1])
        # Revert to normal operations
        skip = False
        if doOnce: break
        # Check to see if button is pressed and quit if so
        if button_pressed():
            if verbose: print('Caught Stop button')
            # Stop running continuous mode on button press also
            continuous = False
            # Wait for button release
            while button_pressed():
                utime.sleep_ms(100)
        # Pause here to let opto button be released so it doesn't get caught again
        while opto_button_pressed():
            utime.sleep_ms(10)
        if len(animList) > 0:
            # Go to next anim in list
            playIndex += 1
            if playIndex >= len(animList): playIndex = 0
            if randomize: playIndex = random.randint(0, len(animList)-1)
        if(verbose): print('At end of loop')
    # Currently no way to get here
    if(verbose): print('At end of run_animation_sequence()')
class LocalSource:
    def __init__(self, filename=None, binblocksize=0, readlock=None):
        self.file = None
        self.binblocksize = binblocksize
        self.readlock = readlock
        if self.readlock: self.readlock.acquire()
        if binblocksize > 0:
            self.file = open(filename, 'rb')
        else:
            self.file = open(filename, 'r')
        if self.readlock: self.readlock.release()
    def readline(self, returnblock=None):
        BLOCKSIZE = 512  # Don't read more than 512 bytes per read
        if self.file is None: return ''
        if self.readlock: self.readlock.acquire()
        if self.binblocksize > 0:
            if returnblock is None:
                returnblock = bytearray(self.binblocksize)
            mv = memoryview(returnblock)
            bytes_read = 0
            n = self.binblocksize
            for i in range(0, n - BLOCKSIZE, BLOCKSIZE):
                bytes_read += self.file.readinto(mv[i:i + BLOCKSIZE])
            if bytes_read < n:
                bytes_read += self.file.readinto(mv[bytes_read:n])
            if bytes_read == 0:
                # At end of file
                return ''
        else:
            returnblock = self.file.readline()
        if self.readlock: self.readlock.release()
        return returnblock
    def close(self):
        if self.file is not None:
            self.file.close()
            self.file = None
def play_one_anim(csvfile, wavefile, idle=False):

        with open(csvfile, 'rb') as source:
            testbyte = source.read(1)
            if testbyte == b'T':
                # Ascii CSV file
                csvformat = CSV
                pass
            elif testbyte == b'0':
                # ASCII hex-encoded file
                csvformat = HEX
                print('Whoops - HEX format no longer supported!!')
                pass
            elif testbyte == b'\x00':
                # Binary encoded file
                csvformat = BIN
                binblocksize = blockSizes[0]
                pass
            else:
                # bad
                if verbose: print('Whoops - Unrecognized control file format:', csvfile)

    # Initialize stats for optional display

    lockTicks = 0
    skips = 0
    readTicks = 0
    splitTicks = 0
    dataTicks = 0
    servodataTicks = 0
    buttonTicks = 0
    garbageTicks = 0
    LEDTicks = 0

    ticks2 = 0
    ticks3 = 0
    ticks4 = 0
    ticks5 = 0

                            else:

                        elif porttypes[i] == PWM:

                                servodataTicks += utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), ticks2)
                            else:
                                # Negative port indicates compacted controls in a single value
                                ticks2 = utime.ticks_us()
                                if csvformat == CSV:
                                    value = int(values[i])

                                    helpers.tables.intsToPWM(vals)
                                servodataTicks += utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), ticks2)
                setTicks += utime.ticks_diff(utime.ticks_us(), ticks1)
                # Make sure all the digital channels are output

            # Read another line from CSV file

# Convert Megatron-LM checkpoint to HuggingFace GPT-SW3 format
import argparse
import os
from os.path import isfile
import torch
from transformers import GPT2Config

def print_structure(name, val, indent=0):
    # Create formatted message with indentation
    if name is None:
        msg = None
    else:
        fmt = "." * max(0, indent - 2) + "# {:" + str(50 - indent) + "s}"
        msg = fmt.format(name)
    
    # Handle different data types
    if isinstance(val, dict):
        if msg is not None:
            print(msg)
        for key in val.keys():
            print_structure(key, val[key], indent + 2)
    elif isinstance(val, torch.Tensor):
        print(msg, ":", val.size())
    else:
        print(msg, ":", val)

def reorder_attention_weights(weight_tensor, num_parts, attention_heads, hidden_dim):
    # Reorganize tensor layout from [num_heads * num_parts * hidden_dim, :] 
    # to [num_parts * num_heads * hidden_dim, :] for compatibility
    original_shape = weight_tensor.size()
    new_shape = (attention_heads, num_parts, hidden_dim) + original_shape[1:]
    weight_tensor = weight_tensor.view(*new_shape)
    weight_tensor = weight_tensor.transpose(0, 1).contiguous()
    weight_tensor = weight_tensor.view(*original_shape)
    return weight_tensor

def transform_megatron_to_hf(state_dict_megatron, config):
    """
    Transforms a Megatron checkpoint to HuggingFace GPT-SW3 format.
    """
    max_positions = config.n_positions
    num_layers = config.n_layer
    vocab_size = config.vocab_size
    num_attention_heads = config.n_head
    hidden_size_per_head = config.n_embd // config.n_head
    
    # Extract and prepare embeddings
    embedding_weights = state_dict_megatron["model.language_model.embedding.word_embeddings.weight"][:vocab_size, :]
    transformed_state_dict = {
        "transformer.wte.weight": embedding_weights,
        "transformer.wpe.weight": state_dict_megatron["model.language_model.embedding.position_embeddings.weight"],
        "transformer.ln_f.weight": state_dict_megatron["model.language_model.encoder.final_layernorm.weight"],
        "transformer.ln_f.bias": state_dict_megatron["model.language_model.encoder.final_layernorm.bias"],
    }
    
    layer_prefix = "model.language_model.encoder.layers."
    for layer_idx in range(num_layers):
        # Create causal attention mask
        causal_mask = torch.tril(torch.ones((max_positions, max_positions), dtype=torch.bool))
        causal_mask = causal_mask.view(1, 1, max_positions, max_positions)
        
        # Add attention mask components
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.attn.bias"] = causal_mask
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.attn.masked_bias"] = torch.tensor(-1e4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        
        # Layer normalization before attention
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.ln_1.weight"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.input_layernorm.weight"]
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.ln_1.bias"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.input_layernorm.bias"]
        
        # Attention weights and biases
        qkv_weight = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.self_attention.query_key_value.weight"]
        qkv_weight = reorder_attention_weights(qkv_weight, 3, num_attention_heads, hidden_size_per_head)
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.attn.c_attn.weight"] = qkv_weight.transpose(0, 1).contiguous()
        
        qkv_bias = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.self_attention.query_key_value.bias"]
        qkv_bias = reorder_attention_weights(qkv_bias, 3, num_attention_heads, hidden_size_per_head)
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.attn.c_attn.bias"] = qkv_bias
        
        # Output projection
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.attn.c_proj.weight"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.self_attention.dense.weight"].transpose(0, 1)
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.attn.c_proj.bias"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.self_attention.dense.bias"]
        
        # Layer normalization after attention
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.ln_2.weight"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.post_attention_layernorm.weight"]
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.ln_2.bias"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.post_attention_layernorm.bias"]
        
        # MLP layers
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.mlp.c_fc.weight"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.mlp.dense_h_to_4h.weight"].transpose(0, 1)
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.mlp.c_fc.bias"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.mlp.dense_h_to_4h.bias"]
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.mlp.c_proj.weight"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.mlp.dense_4h_to_h.weight"].transpose(0, 1)
        transformed_state_dict[f"transformer.h.{layer_idx}.mlp.c_proj.bias"] = state_dict_megatron[f"{layer_prefix}{layer_idx}.mlp.dense_4h_to_h.bias"]
    
    # LM head shares weights with word embeddings
    transformed_state_dict["lm_head.weight"] = embedding_weights
    
    return transformed_state_dict

def update_config hf_config, megatron_config):
    """Update HuggingFace config with values from Megatron config."""
    hf_config.vocab_size = 64000
    hf_config.n_positions = megatron_config["encoder_seq_length"]
    hf_config.n_embd = megatron_config["hidden_size"]
    hf_config.n_layer = megatron_config["num_layers"]
    hf_config.n_head = megatron_config["num_attention_heads"]
    hf_config.n_inner = megatron_config["ffn_hidden_size"]
    hf_config.activation_function = "gelu"
    hf_config.resid_pdrop = 0.1
    hf_config.embd_pdrop = 0.1
    hf_config.attn_pdrop = 0.1
    hf_config.layer_norm_epsilon = megatron_config["layernorm_epsilon"]  # 1e-5
    hf_config.initializer_range = megatron_config["init_method_std"]  # 0.02
    hf_config.apply_query_key_layer_scaling = megatron_config["apply_query_key_layer_scaling"]  # True
    hf_config.normalize_attention_scores = True
    hf_config.use_cache = True
    
    # Token ID configuration based on model size
    if megatron_config["hidden_size"] == 4096:
        hf_config.bos_token_id = 1  # 6.7B model uses different tokenizer
        hf_config.eos_token_id = 1
        hf_config.pad_token_id = 0  # <unk>
    else:
        hf_config.bos_token_id = 2  # <s>
        hf_config.eos_token_id = 3  # </s>
        hf_config.pad_token_id = 0  # <pad>
    
    return hf_config

def main(args):
    print(args)
    checkpoint_path = args.checkpoint_path
    output_dir = args.save_path
    
    # Verify checkpoint exists
    if not isfile(checkpoint_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"ERROR! could not find file {checkpoint_path}")
    
    # Load the checkpoint
    checkpoint = torch.load(checkpoint_path, map_location="cpu")

from .util.tree_search import Node

def search(initial_state, target_state):
    """Iterative deepening depth-first search implementation"""
    max_depth = 0
    solution_path = None
    
    def limited_search(current_node):
        # Check if current node meets the goal condition
        if current_node.is_goal(target_state):
            return current_node
        
        # Only explore deeper if we haven't reached the current depth limit
        if current_node.depth < max_depth:
            current_node.expand()
            for child_node in current_node.children:
                recursive_result = limited_search(child_node)
                if recursive_result is not None:
                    return recursive_result
        return None
    
    # Continue increasing depth until a solution is found
    while solution_path is None:
        start_node = Node(initial_state)
        solution_path = limited_search(start_node)
        max_depth += 1
    
    # Reconstruct the path from solution to root
    path_states = []
    path_states.append(solution_path.state)
    
    # Traverse parent references to collect all states
    for ancestor in solution_path.parents():
        path_states.append(ancestor.state)
    
    # Reverse to get root-to-goal order
    path_states.reverse()
    return path_states

def execute_comet_analysis():

        status.warn("Please open the ROI Manager tool (Analyze > Tools > ROI Manager...).")
        return False
    
    rois = roi_manager.getRoisAsArray()
    if len(rois) == 0:
        status.warn("No ROIs present in the ROI Manager.")
        return False
    
    # Save ROIs if requested
    if save_roi_flag:
        roi_save_path = os.path.splitext(source_file)[0] + ".ROI.zip"
        roi_manager.runCommand("Save", roi_save_path)
    
    # Initialize results table
    results_table = ResultsTable()
    
    # Process each ROI to compute metrics
    for index, roi in enumerate(rois):
        # Normalize coordinates to ensure consistent ordering
        left_x = min(roi.x1, roi.x2)
        right_x = max(roi.x1, roi.x2)
        top_y = min(roi.y1, roi.y2)
        bottom_y = max(roi.y1, roi.y2)
        
        # Compute run parameters
        distance_traveled = bottom_y - top_y
        time_elapsed = right_x - left_x
        
        # Avoid division by zero
        if time_elapsed != 0:
            velocity = distance_traveled / time_elapsed
        else:
            velocity = 0.0
        
        # Populate results table
        results_table.incrementCounter()
        results_table.addValue("Track ID", index + 1)
        results_table.addValue("Track Length (um)", distance_traveled)
        results_table.addValue("Track duration (s)", time_elapsed)
        results_table.addValue("Track speed (um/s)", velocity)
    
    # Save and display results
    output_path = os.path.splitext(source_file)[0] + ".Results.csv"
    results_table.save(output_path)
    results_table.show('Comet Analysis Results for "%s"' % image_name)

# Fuzzy matching and distance-based rules for two-dimensional coordinates

from extensions.rules import base

class Within(base.CoordTwoDimRule):
    description = 'lies within {{d|Real}} kilometers of {{p|CoordTwoDim}}'
    
    # Implementation uses haversine formula to compute great-circle distance
    # between two points on Earth given latitude and longitude in degrees
    
    def evaluate(self, answer, interaction_answer):
        # Extract coordinates: (lat, lon) in degrees
        lat1, lon1 = answer['lat'], answer['lon']
        lat2, lon2 = interaction_answer['lat'], interaction_answer['lon']
        
        # Convert degrees to radians
        from math import radians, sin, cos, asin, sqrt
        
        R = 6371  # Earth's radius in kilometers
        
        phi1, phi2 = radians(lat1), radians(lat2)
        dphi = radians(lat2 - lat1)
        dlambda = radians(lon2 - lon1)
        
        a = sin(dphi/2)**2 + cos(phi1) * cos(phi2) * sin(dlambda/2)**2
        c = 2 * asin(sqrt(a))
        
        distance = R * c
        threshold = self._get_param('d')
        
        return distance <= threshold


class NotWithin(base.CoordTwoDimRule):
    description = 'lies more than {{d|Real}} kilometers away from {{p|CoordTwoDim}}'
    
    def evaluate(self, answer, interaction_answer):
        # Reuse logic from Within rule but invert the result
        within_rule = Within()
        return not within_rule.evaluate(answer, interaction_answer)


class FuzzyMatches(base.CoordTwoDimRule):
    description = 'approximately matches one of {{training_data|ListOfCoordTwoDim}}'
    
    # Uses Euclidean distance in normalized coordinate space for approximate matching
    # This is a simplified approximation suitable for small geographic regions
    
    def evaluate(self, answer, interaction_answer):
        training_points = self._get_param('training_data')
        if not training_points:
            return False
            
        # Normalize coordinates to reduce scale differences
        # Use simple scaling factor based on average latitude
        avg_lat = sum(p['lat'] for p in training_points) / len(training_points)
        lat_scale = 111.0  # km per degree latitude (approx.)
        lon_scale = 111.0 * cos(radians(avg_lat)) if avg_lat else 111.0
        
        ans_x = answer['lat'] * lat_scale
        ans_y = answer['lon'] * lon_scale
        
        for point in training_points:
            train_x = point['lat'] * lat_scale
            train_y = point['lon'] * lon_scale
            
            # Compute Euclidean distance in scaled space
            dist = ((ans_x - train_x)**2 + (ans_y - train_y)**2)**0.5
            
            # Threshold can be tuned; here using 5 km equivalent in scaled units
            if dist <= 5.0:
                return True
                
        return False

# Virgil Security SDK wrapper class implementation

from virgil_sdk.api import IdentitiesManager
from virgil_sdk.api import VirgilContext
from virgil_sdk.api.card_manager import CardManager
from virgil_sdk.api.key_manager import KeyManager

class VirgilSecurity(object):
    """High-level interface for interacting with Virgil Security services.
    
    This class simplifies cryptographic operations by encapsulating key and card management,
    identity handling, and context configuration through VirgilKey and VirgilCard entities.
    """
    
    def __init__(
            self,
            token=None,  # type: str
            ctx=None     # type: VirgilContext
    ):
        # type: (...) -> None
        self.__token = token
        self._internal_context = ctx
        self.private_keys = KeyManager(self.__get_context())
        self.certificates = CardManager(self.__get_context())
        self.user_identities = IdentitiesManager(self.__get_context())
    
    @property
    def __get_context(self):
        # type: () -> VirgilContext
        """Lazy-initializes and returns the VirgilContext instance."""
        if not self._internal_context:
            self._internal_context = VirgilContext(self.__token)
        return self._internal_context

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(app_label)

def execute():
    import argparse
    import paste.deploy
    from ckanofworms import environment, model
    
    # Set up command-line argument parsing
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('config_file', help='absolute or relative path to CKAN-of-Worms Paste config file')
    parser.add_argument('-d', '--debug', action='store_true', dest='debug_mode', help='enable detailed logging output')
    
    parsed_args = parser.parse_args()
    
    # Configure logging level based on verbosity flag
    log_level = logging.DEBUG if parsed_args.debug_mode else logging.WARNING
    logging.basicConfig(level=log_level, stream=sys.stdout)
    
    # Load CKAN configuration using PasteDeploy
    app_config = paste.deploy.appconfig(f'config:{os.path.abspath(parsed_args.config_file)}')
    environment.load_environment(app_config.global_conf, app_config.local_conf)
    
    # Retrieve or initialize upgrade status record
    current_status = model.Status.find_one()
    if current_status is None:
        current_status = model.Status()
    
    # Perform index cleanup and update upgrade tracking
    perform_index_cleanup(current_status)
    
    return 0

def perform_index_cleanup(status_record):
    db_client = objects.Wrapper.db
    # Iterate through all collections in the database
    for collection_identifier in db_client.collection_names():
        # Skip system collections (those starting with 'system.')
        if collection_identifier.startswith('system.'):
            continue
        # Remove all indexes from non-system collections
        db_client[collection_identifier].drop_indexes()
    
    # Update upgrade status if this is a new or newer upgrade
    if status_record.last_applied_migration is None or status_record.last_applied_migration < app_label:
        status_record.last_applied_migration = app_label
        status_record.save()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(execute())

# Reimplementation of OpenFlow Hello message components with equivalent behavior

from enum import Enum
from pyof.foundation.base import GenericMessage, GenericStruct
from pyof.foundation.basic_types import BinaryData, FixedTypeList, UBInt16
from pyof.v0x04.common.header import Header, Type

__all__ = ('OpenFlowHello', 'ElemHeaderBase', 'ElementType',
           'VersionBitmapElem', 'ElementCollection')


class ElementType(Enum):
    """Supported OpenFlow hello element kinds."""
    VERSION_BITMAP_INDICATOR = 1


class ElemHeaderBase(GenericStruct):
    """Base class for any hello element header."""
    kind = UBInt16(enum_ref=ElementType)
    size = UBInt16()

    def __init__(self, kind=None, size=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.kind = kind
        self.size = size


class ElementCollection(FixedTypeList):
    """Container holding multiple hello elements."""
    def __init__(self, entries=None):
        super().__init__(pyof_class=ElemHeaderBase, items=entries)


class OpenFlowHello(GenericMessage):
    """Represents an OpenFlow OFPT_HELLO message."""
    header = Header(message_type=Type.OFPT_HELLO, length=8)
    payload_elements = ElementCollection()

    def __init__(self, transaction_id=None, payload_elements=None):
        super().__init__(transaction_id)
        self.payload_elements = payload_elements if payload_elements is not None else []


class VersionBitmapElem(ElemHeaderBase):
    """A specific hello element carrying version support info."""
    supported_versions = BinaryData()

    def __init__(self, supported_versions=b''):
        super().__init__(
            kind=ElementType.VERSION_BITMAP_INDICATOR,
            size=None
        )
        self.supported_versions = supported_versions

_error_list = []

def log_error(function_name, message):
    """Collect an error/warning message and display it on stderr.
    
    Parameters:
    function_name -- usually the calling function or module identifier
    message -- descriptive error or warning text
    
    Returns:
    None
    
    Use this function whenever an issue needs to be logged; then call
    write_errors_to_file before program termination.
    
    """
    
    if function_name is None:
        function_name = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    
    formatted_message = f"{function_name}: {message}"
    _error_list.append(formatted_message)
    sys.stderr.write(formatted_message + "\n")

def write_errors_to_file(data_file, variable_name="ExecutionErrors"):
    """Write all collected messages to a data file.
    
    Parameters:
    data_file -- an open DTDataFile object
    variable_name -- defaults to "ExecutionErrors" for DataTank compatibility
    
    Returns:
    None
    
    The saved content will appear in DataTank's Messages panel.
    
    """
    
    if _error_list:
        data_file.write_anonymous(_error_list, variable_name)

def sort_array_with_rust(array):
    """
    Sort a NumPy array in-place using the Rust quicksort implementation.
    Supports signed/unsigned integers (8/16/32/64-bit) and floating-point numbers (32/64-bit).
    """
    data_ptr = ctypes.c_void_p(array.ctypes.data)
    element_count = len(array)
    
    # Dispatch to appropriate FFI function based on array dtype
    if array.dtype == np.int8:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_i8(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.int16:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_i16(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.int32:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_i32(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.int64:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_i64(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.uint8:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_u8(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.uint16:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_u16(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.uint32:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_u32(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.uint64:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_u64(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.float32:
        rust_shared_lib.ffi_quicksort_f32(data_ptr, element_count)
    elif array.dtype == np.float64:

# Calculate the number of operations needed to reduce all tree heights to zero

def pluck_heights(heights):
    # Find the largest and second largest distinct values
    unique_heights = list(set(heights))
    
    if len(unique_heights) < 2:
        # All elements are the same or only one element exists
        return [0] * len(heights)
    
    # Sort in descending order to get top two distinct values
    sorted_heights = sorted(unique_heights, reverse=True)
    max_val = sorted_heights[0]
    second_max_val = sorted_heights[1]
    
    # If all values are equal (shouldn't happen due to set, but safety check)
    if max_val == second_max_val:
        return [0] * len(heights)
    
    # Reduce only the maximum values by the difference
    diff = max_val - second_max_val
    return [h - diff if h == max_val else h for h in heights]

def count_operations(heights):
    counter = 0
    # Continue until all heights are zero
    while any(h > 0 for h in heights):
        heights = pluck_heights(heights)
        counter += 1
    return counter - 1 if counter > 0 else 0

import logging
from threading import Condition, Lock
from aquilon.locks import LockQueue, LockKey
from aquilon.exceptions_ import InternalError
from aquilon.server.logger import CLIENT_INFO

LOGGER = logging.getLogger('aquilon.server.locks')

# Global lock queue instance for centralized lock management across the broker
lock_queue = LockQueue()

# Compile operations are logically divided into four sequential stages:
# 1 - Read plenary and profile templates to determine changes needed
# 2 - Persist modified plenary and profile templates
# 3 - Access required templates (plenary, profile, cached profile, domain) for compilation
# 4 - Output compiled profiles and cache templates
#
# If a template is deemed unchanged during stage 1, it must not be rewritten in stage 2.
#
# Although named after "compile", this lock primarily guards the final output state
# of generated profiles, which is the critical artifact we aim to keep consistent.

class CompileLockKey(LockKey):
    def __init__(self, domain=None, profile=None,
                 logger=LOGGER, loglevel=CLIENT_INFO):
        """Construct a compile lock key specifying domain and target profile.
        The profile may represent either a host or cluster.
        """
        self.domain_name = domain
        self.target_profile = profile
        
        # Build ordered components for the lock identifier
        key_parts = ["compile"]
        
        if self.domain_name:
            key_parts.append(self.domain_name)
            if self.target_profile:
                key_parts.append(self.target_profile)
        elif self.target_profile:
            raise InternalError("Compile lock requested for '%s' without specifying domain." %
                                self.target_profile)
        
        super().__init__(key_parts, logger=logger, loglevel=loglevel)

class DeleteLockKey(LockKey):
    """Lock for broad deletion operations."""
    def __init__(self, group=None, logger=LOGGER, loglevel=CLIENT_INFO):
        self.group_name = group
        key_parts = ["delete"]
        if self.group_name:
            key_parts.append(self.group_name)
        super().__init__(key_parts, logger=logger, loglevel=loglevel)

class RefreshLockKey(LockKey):
    """Locks used by data synchronization commands."""
    def __init__(self, source=None, logger=LOGGER, loglevel=CLIENT_INFO):
        self.source_data = source
        key_parts = ["sync"]
        if self.source_data:
            key_parts.append(self.source_data)
        super().__init__(key_parts, logger=logger, loglevel=loglevel)

def test_loudness_ecma():
    """Test function for the Loudness_ecma calculation

    at 60 dB SPL yields a phon value close to 60, within tolerance.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    None

    -------
    None
    """

    signal, sample_rate = sine_wave_generator(
        fs=48000,
        duration=1.0,
        spl_value=60,
        frequency=1000,
    )
    
    # Compute loudness over time
    loudness_results = comp_loudness(signal, validation=False)
    time_vector = loudness_results[1]
    
    # Extract first column (time-varying loudness in phons)
    phon_values = time_vector[:, 0]
    
    # Calculate average phon value
    avg_phon = mean(phon_values)
    
    # Convert to sones for verification (optional, but keeps consistency)

    # Assert that the result is within acceptable tolerance

import argparse
import os
import re

def batch_rename_files(path, simulate=True):
    if not simulate:
        print("Executing actual renaming...")
    else:
        print("Simulating changes only...")
        
    entries = [entry for entry in os.listdir(path) if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, entry))]
    
    for current_file in entries:
        # Sanitize filename: replace non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphen, dot, comma, underscore)
        sanitized = re.sub(r'[^0-9a-zA-Z\-.,_]', '_', current_file)
        # Collapse multiple underscores into one
        sanitized = re.sub(r'_+', '_', sanitized)
        # Restore hyphenated words that were split by special chars
        sanitized = re.sub(r'-_-', '-', sanitized)
        # Remove leading/trailing underscores and trailing dots
        sanitized = re.sub(r'(^_|_$|\.+$)', '', sanitized)
        
        full_current = os.path.join(path, current_file)
        full_new = os.path.join(path, sanitized)
        
        if simulate:
            print(f"{current_file} -> {sanitized}")
        else:
            os.rename(full_current, full_new)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Rename files in a directory to sanitize names.")
    parser.add_argument('target_directory', type=str, help="Path to the directory containing files to rename")
    parser.add_argument('-x', '--execute', default=False, action='store_true', 
                        help="When omitted, only shows what would be renamed (dry run). Use to apply changes.")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    batch_rename_files(arguments.target_directory, arguments.execute)

# Reimplementation of grammar parsing logic with modified structure and control flow

from .ast import ASTNode
from .languages import ParseTreeChar, make_sppf
from .linguify_grammar import linguify_grammar_file
from viper.lexer import Lexeme
from os.path import join, dirname
from typing import List

class GrammarParser:
    def __init__(self, grammar_path: str):
        self.grammar_file = grammar_path
        self.rule_set = linguify_grammar_file(self.grammar_file)
    
    def extract_parse_tree(self, rule_name: str, token_stream: List[Lexeme]) -> ASTNode:
        target_language = self.rule_set[rule_name]
        parsed_sppf = make_sppf(target_language, token_stream)
        
        # Handle different parsing outcomes
        if not parsed_sppf:
            raise RuntimeError("Parsing failed: no valid parse trees found.")
        
        tree_count = len(parsed_sppf)
        if tree_count == 1:
            single_tree = parsed_sppf[0]
            
            # Validate parse tree node type
            if not isinstance(single_tree, ParseTreeChar):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected parse tree structure: {single_tree}")
            
            extracted_token = single_tree.token
            
            # Ensure extracted token is an AST node
            if not isinstance(extracted_token, ASTNode):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid AST node in parse result: {extracted_token}")
            
            return extracted_token
        else:
            # Ambiguity detected
            raise RuntimeError(f"Ambiguous parse: {tree_count} possible parse trees found.")

# Initialize global grammar instance

from .base import Base
import requests

class Config(Base):
    """Fetch and display basic nio configuration information"""
    
    def __init__(self, options, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(options, *args, **kwargs)
        
        # Determine resource type based on command-line options
        if self.options['services']:
            self._resource = 'services'
            self._resource_name = self.options.get('<service-name>', '')
        elif self.options['blocks']:
            self._resource = 'blocks'
            self._resource_name = self.options.get('<block-name>', '')
        else:
            self._resource = ''
            self._resource_name = ''
    
    def run(self):
        # Construct the full URL path
        url_path = f"{self._resource}/{self._resource_name}" if self._resource else ""
        full_url = self._base_url.format(url_path)
        
        # Make authenticated HTTP GET request
        try:
            response = requests.get(full_url, auth=self._auth)
            response.raise_for_status()  # Raise exception for HTTP errors
            
            # Parse and display JSON response
            config_data = response.json()
            print(config_data)
            
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            print(f"Request failed: {e}")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"JSON parsing error: {e}")

import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import svd
from fasttsne import _TSNE as TSNE

def fast_tsne(data, pca_components=None, embedding_dim=2, neighbor_scale=30., accuracy_param=0.5):
    """
    Apply Barnes-Hut approximation of t-SNE on input data.
    @param data         Input dataset (samples x features).
    @param pca_components  If specified, reduce dimensionality using PCA to this number.
    @param embedding_dim   Target dimensionality of the embedding (typically 2).
    @param neighbor_scale  Controls the balance between local and global structure.
    @param accuracy_param  Approximation parameter: lower = more accurate but slower.
    """
    n_samples, n_features = data.shape
    
    # Center data if PCA is used
    if pca_components is None:
        processed_data = data.copy()
    else:
        # Mean-centering
        centered_data = data - np.mean(data, axis=0)
        
        # Compute covariance matrix for efficient PCA
        cov_matrix = np.dot(centered_data.T, centered_data) / n_samples
        
        # Perform SVD decomposition
        U, singular_vals, Vt = svd(cov_matrix, full_matrices=False)
        
        # Project onto top principal components
        projection_matrix = U[:, :pca_components]
        processed_data = np.dot(centered_data, projection_matrix)
    
    # Initialize and run t-SNE
    tsne_model = TSNE()
    embedding = tsne_model.run(
        processed_data, 
        n_samples, 
        processed_data.shape[1], 
        embedding_dim, 
        neighbor_scale, 
        accuracy_param
    )
    return embedding

def update_message_metadata(apps: StateApps, schema_editor: DatabaseSchemaEditor) -> None:
    Message = apps.get_model('zerver', 'Message')
    
    # Iterate through all messages in the database
    for msg in Message.objects.all():
        # Determine if message has attachments by checking related attachment records
        has_attachment = msg.attachment_set.exists()
        
        # Parse the rendered HTML content to extract link and image information
        html_tree = lxml.html.fromstring(msg.rendered_content)
        
        # Check for hyperlinks in the message content
        has_link = any(True for _ in html_tree.xpath("//a"))
        
        # Check for inline images by looking for elements with specific CSS class
        has_image = any(True for _ in html_tree.find_class("message_inline_image"))
        
        # Skip database update if current values match computed values
        if (msg.has_link == has_link and 
            msg.has_attachment == has_attachment and 
            msg.has_image == has_image):
            continue
            
        # Update only the necessary fields to avoid unnecessary writes
        msg.has_link = has_link
        msg.has_attachment = has_attachment
        msg.has_image = has_image
        msg.save(update_fields=['has_link', 'has_attachment', 'has_image'])

import requests
import os
import shutil

# Imgur application Client ID - please provide your own
CLIENT_ID = ''
# Base directory where albums will be saved
BASE_DIR = 'Imgur Albums\\'

def fetch_album_images(album_identifier):
    """ 
    (str) -> list of str
    Retrieves all image URLs from an Imgur album given its ID.
    Saves each image to a dedicated subdirectory and returns the list of URLs processed.
    """
    # Create album-specific folder path
    album_folder_path = BASE_DIR + album_identifier + '\\'
    
    # Ensure the directory exists; create it if not
    if not os.path.exists(album_folder_path):
        os.makedirs(album_folder_path)
    
    downloaded_urls = []
    print(f'Fetching Album: {album_identifier}')
    
    # Construct API endpoint and headers for authentication
    api_url = f'https://api.imgur.com/3/album/{album_identifier}'
    auth_headers = {'Authorization': f'Client-Id {CLIENT_ID}'}
    
    # Make request to Imgur API
    response = requests.get(api_url, headers=auth_headers)
    album_data = response.json()
    
    # Handle API errors
    if not album_data.get('success', False):
        error_message = album_data.get('data', {}).get('error', 'Unknown error')
        raise Exception(error_message)
    
    # Extract image links from the album data
    for img in album_data['data']['images']:
        downloaded_urls.append(img['link'])
    
    # Download each image and save to disk
    for url in downloaded_urls:
        # Fetch image with streaming enabled
        image_response = requests.get(url, stream=True)
        
        # Extract filename from URL (after 'com/')
        filename_start = url.find('com/') + 4
        filename = url[filename_start:]
        file_path = os.path.join(album_folder_path, filename)
        
        # Write image to file using shutil for efficiency
        with open(file_path, 'wb') as output_file:
            shutil.copyfileobj(image_response.raw, output_file)
    
    return downloaded_urls

# UPnP port mapping utilities for Raiden network

import miniupnpc
from ethereum import slogging

MAX_PORT_NUMBER = 65535
SERVICE_IDENTIFIER = "raiden-network udp service"
logger = slogging.getLogger(__name__)

def establish_connection():
    """Attempt to establish connection with the router.
    
    Returns:
        upnp_obj (miniupnpc.UPnP): connected UPnP instance or None
        gateway_info (str): router connection details or None
    """
    upnp_obj = miniupnpc.UPnP()
    upnp_obj.discoverdelay = 200
    
    found_devices = upnp_obj.discover()
    if found_devices > 1:
        logger.warning("detected multiple UPnP devices", device_count=found_devices)
    elif found_devices == 0:
        logger.error("no UPnP devices detected")
        return None, None
    
    gateway_info = upnp_obj.selectigd()
    logger.debug("connection established", gateway=gateway_info)
    
    # Validate local address
    if upnp_obj.lanaddr == '0.0.0.0':
        logger.error("failed to determine local IP address")
        return None, None
    
    # Validate external address
    external_ip = upnp_obj.externalipaddress()
    if external_ip in ('0.0.0.0', None):
        logger.error("failed to determine external IP address")
        return None, None
    
    return upnp_obj, gateway_info

def activate_port_mapping(internal_service_port, start_external_port=None):
    """Configure UPnP port forwarding for the Raiden service.
    
    Args:
        internal_service_port (int): port where Raiden service listens
        start_external_port (int): first external port to try (default: internal_service_port)
    
    Returns:
        tuple(str, int) or None: (external_ip, external_port) if successful
    """
    if start_external_port is None:
        start_external_port = internal_service_port
    
    upnp_obj, gateway = establish_connection()
    if upnp_obj is None:
        return None
    
    def attempt_mapping(internal, external):
        return upnp_obj.addportmapping(
            internal,
            'UDP',
            upnp_obj.lanaddr,
            external,
            SERVICE_IDENTIFIER,
            ''
        )
    
    current_external_port = start_external_port
    mapping_created = attempt_mapping(internal_service_port, current_external_port)
    
    while not mapping_created and current_external_port <= MAX_PORT_NUMBER:
        current_external_port += 1
        mapping_created = attempt_mapping(internal_service_port, current_external_port)
    
    if mapping_created:
        logger.info("UPnP port mapping configured",
                   local=f"{upnp_obj.lanaddr}:{internal_service_port}",
                   public=f"{upnp_obj.externalipaddress()}:{current_external_port}")
        return (upnp_obj.externalipaddress(), current_external_port)
    else:
        logger.error("failed to configure port mapping", gateway='FIXME')
        return None

def deactivate_port_mapping(internal_service_port):
    """Remove existing UPnP port mapping for the specified internal port.
    
    Args:
        internal_service_port (int): previously mapped internal port
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if removal was successful, False otherwise
    """
    upnp_obj, gateway = establish_connection()
    if upnp_obj is None:
        return False
    
    existing_mapping = upnp_obj.getspecificportmapping(internal_service_port, 'UDP')
    if existing_mapping is None:
        logger.error("no existing port mapping found", gateway=gateway)
        return False
    
    deletion_success = upnp_obj.deleteportmapping(internal_service_port, 'UDP')
    if deletion_success:
        logger.info("port mapping successfully removed", gateway=gateway)
        return True
    else:
        logger.warning("failed to remove port mapping - manual cleanup may be needed", gateway=gateway)
        return False

# Custom fiscal position tax mapping logic

from openerp import models, api, fields

class AccountFiscalPosition(models.Model):
    _inherit = 'account.fiscal.position'
    
    @api.v7
    def map_taxes(self, cr, uid, fposition_id, taxes, context=None):
        # Call parent method first to get base mapping
        base_result = super(AccountFiscalPosition, self).map_tax(
            cr, uid, fposition_id, taxes, context=context)
        
        # Collect destination tax IDs for entries without source tax
        dest_tax_ids = [
            tax_rec.tax_dest_id.id 
            for tax_rec in fposition_id.tax_ids 
            if not tax_rec.tax_src_id
        ]
        
        # Merge with existing results using set union to avoid duplicates
        final_result = list(set(base_result) | set(dest_tax_ids))
        return final_result
    
    @api.v8     # noqa
    def map_taxes(self, taxes):
        # Get initial mapping from parent class
        base_result = super(AccountFiscalPosition, self).map_tax(taxes)
        
        # Find destination taxes where no source tax is specified
        dest_tax_ids = [
            tax_record.tax_dest_id.id 
            for tax_record in self.tax_ids 
            if not tax_record.tax_src_id
        ]
        
        # Extend result with records corresponding to the collected IDs
        additional_records = base_result.browse(dest_tax_ids)
        combined_result = base_result + additional_records
        return combined_result

class AccountFiscalPositionTax(models.Model):

    # Make source tax optional
    tax_src_id = fields.Many2one(required=False)

import asyncio
import discord
import textwrap
from discord.ext import commands

async def split_and_send(bot, message_content, destination, user, max_chunks: int = 5, chunk_size: int = 2000):
    """A helper function to split long messages and send them appropriately."""
    if not all([bot, message_content, destination]):
        return False

    # Split the message into chunks based on character limit
    chunks = textwrap.wrap(message_content, chunk_size, break_long_words=True, replace_whitespace=False)

    if not chunks:
        return False

    # Ensure DM channel exists for the user
    if not user.dm_channel:
        await user.create_dm()
    
    dm_channel = user.dm_channel

    # If too many chunks and not already sending to DM, notify and redirect
    if len(chunks) > max_chunks and dm_channel.id != destination.id:
        await destination.send(f"This message is quite long ({len(chunks)} parts), so I'll DM it instead.")
        destination = user

    # Send each chunk sequentially
    for chunk in chunks:
        await destination.send(chunk)

    return True

# Custom USSD transport implementation based on HTTP RPC base class
from vumi.transports.httprpc import HttpRpcTransport

class DmarkUssdConfiguration(HttpRpcTransport.CONFIG_CLASS):
    """Configuration settings specific to the Dmark USSD transport."""
    
class DmarkUssdService(HttpRpcTransport):
    """USSD service implementation for Dmark via HTTP protocol.
    
    Upon receiving a USSD request, Dmark sends an HTTP GET request containing:
    * ``transactionId``: Unique identifier for the session (string).
    * ``msisdn``: Originating phone number (string).
    * ``ussdServiceCode``: Target USSD service code (string).
    * ``transactionTime``: Unix timestamp (UTC) when Dmark received the request.
    * ``ussdRequestString``: Full content of the USSD input (string).
    * ``creationTime``: Optional Unix timestamp (UTC) when the request was created
      by the mobile network (may be unreliable).
      
    The transport supports JSON or form-encoded responses. Successful processing
    requires returning HTTP 200; any other status indicates failure.
    
    This implementation returns JSON with:
    * ``responseString``: Message displayed to the user.
    * ``action``: Either 'end' (terminate session) or 'request' (continue interaction).
    
    **Sample JSON response**:
    .. sourcecode: javascript
       {
         "responseString": "Hello from Vumi!",
         "action": "end"
       }
    """
    CONFIG_CLASS = DmarkUssdConfiguration
    
    def process_inbound_ussd(self, msgid, request):
        raise NotImplementedError("Sub-classes must implement process_inbound_ussd.")
        
    def process_outbound_ussd(self, message):
        self.log("DmarkUssdService processing %s" % (message,))
        
        required_fields = ['in_reply_to', 'content']
        missing = [field for field in required_fields if field not in message.payload]
        
        if missing:
            return self.reject_message(message, missing)
            
        # Send response back to the original request
        self.complete_request(
            message.payload['in_reply_to'],
            message.payload['content'].encode('utf-8')
        )
        
        # Acknowledge successful processing
        return self.publish_ack(
            user_message_id=message['message_id'],
            sent_message_id=message['message_id']
        )

def test_write_pickled_dict_to_file_v2(tmpdir):
    # Create filesystem and file path
    filesystem, filepath = open_fs(str(tmpdir)), 'data.pkl'
    
    # Initialize writer and execution context
    serializer = PickleWriter(path=filepath)
    execution_context = NodeExecutionContext(serializer, services={'fs': filesystem})
    
    # Send special tokens and data bags
    execution_context.write(BEGIN, Bag({'foo': 'bar'}), Bag({'foo': 'baz', 'ignore': 'this'}), END)
    
    # Execute the node lifecycle
    execution_context.start()
    execution_context.step()
    execution_context.step()
    execution_context.stop()
    
    # Verify output file contents
    with filesystem.open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
        content = pickle.loads(f.read())
    assert content == {'foo': 'bar'}
    
    # Ensure internal file attribute is not exposed
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        getattr(execution_context, 'file')

def test_read_pickled_list_from_file_v2(tmpdir):
    # Setup filesystem and input file
    filesystem, input_path = open_fs(str(tmpdir)), 'input_data.pkl'
    
    # Write test data to file
    test_data = [
        ['a', 'b', 'c'], 
        ['a foo', 'b foo', 'c foo'], 
        ['a bar', 'b bar', 'c bar']
    ]
    with filesystem.open(input_path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(pickle.dumps(test_data))
    
    # Initialize reader and capturing context
    deserializer = PickleReader(path=input_path)
    context = CapturingNodeExecutionContext(deserializer, services={'fs': filesystem})
    
    # Execute reading process
    context.start()
    context.write(BEGIN, Bag(), END)
    context.step()
    context.stop()
    
    # Validate number of outputs
    assert len(context.send.mock_calls) == 2
    
    # Check first output
    first_call_args, first_call_kwargs = context.send.call_args_list[0]
    assert len(first_call_args) == 1 and len(first_call_kwargs) == 0
    first_result = first_call_args[0].args[0]
    assert first_result == {
        'a': 'a foo',
        'b': 'b foo',
        'c': 'c foo',
    }
    
    # Check second output
    second_call_args, second_call_kwargs = context.send.call_args_list[1]
    assert len(second_call_args) == 1 and len(second_call_kwargs) == 0
    second_result = second_call_args[0].args[0]
    assert second_result == {
        'a': 'a bar',
        'b': 'b bar',
        'c': 'c bar',
    }

import copy
import pytest
from ..core import Document, NotMutable

def test_immutable_operations():
    doc = Document({'a': 1})
    
    # Test various mutation attempts that should raise NotMutable exception
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc['a'] = 2  # Modify existing key
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc['b'] = 3  # Add new key
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.setdefault('a', 2)  # setdefault on existing key
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.setdefault('c', 4)  # setdefault on non-existing key
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        del doc['a']  # Delete key
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.pop('a')  # Pop key
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.popitem()  # Pop item
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.clear()  # Clear dictionary
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.update({'a': 5})  # Update existing key via update()
        
    with pytest.raises(NotMutable):
        doc.update({'d': 6})  # Add new key via update()

    # Ensure original remains unchanged

from garage import asserts
from sqlalchemy.schema import CreateIndex

def add_index_if_not_exists(index, engine):
    # Bypassing the limitation where `sqlalchemy.Index.create()` doesn't support `if_not_exists`
    # by manually modifying the generated SQL statement.
    compiled_stmt = str(CreateIndex(index).compile(engine))
    modified_stmt = compiled_stmt.replace('CREATE INDEX', 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS', 1)
    asserts.postcond('IF NOT EXISTS' in modified_stmt, modified_stmt)
    return modified_stmt

def ensure_single_row(rows):
    first_row = rows.fetchone()
    if first_row is None:
        raise KeyError("No rows found")
    second_row = rows.fetchone()
    if second_row is not None:
        raise KeyError("Multiple rows found when exactly one was expected")
    return first_row

def insert_with_ignore(conn, table, values_dict):
    conn.execute(table.insert().prefix_with('OR IGNORE'), values_dict)

# Custom database manager implementation for handling ORM operations

from typing import Dict, Type, Union, List, Any
from ..database import BaseModel, db


class DatabaseHandler:
    def __init__(self):
        # Initialize internal references if needed
        self._db = db
        self._model_class: Type[BaseModel] = BaseModel

    def create_entry(self, **data) -> BaseModel:
        """Insert a new record into the database.
        
        Args:
            data: Key-value pairs representing column values for the new record.
            
        Returns:
            BaseModel: The newly created and persisted database object.
        """
        instance = self._model_class(**data)
        self._db.session.add(instance)
        self._db.session.commit()
        return instance

    def find_one(self, **filters) -> Union[BaseModel, None]:
        """Retrieve a single record matching specified criteria.
        
        Args:
            filters: Column-value pairs to filter the query.
            
        Returns:
            BaseModel or None: The first matching record or None if not found.
        """
        result = self._db.session.query(self._model_class).filter_by(**filters).first()
        return result

    def find_all(self) -> List[BaseModel]:
        """Fetch all records of the model type.
        
        Returns:
            List[BaseModel]: A list containing all records.
        """
        return self._db.session.query(self._model_class).all()

    def remove(self, **criteria) -> None:
        """Delete a record (or records) based on provided filters.
        
        Args:
            criteria: Column-value pairs used to identify records to delete.
        """
        target_records = self.find_all_filtered(**criteria)
        for record in target_records:
            self._db.session.delete(record)
        self._db.session.commit()

    def update_records(self, search_params: Dict[str, Any], updates: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Update existing records with new values.
        
        Args:
            search_params: Filters to locate records to update.
            updates: Dictionary of column names and their new values.
        """
        self._db.session.query(self._model_class).filter_by(**search_params).update(updates)
        self._db.session.commit()

    def exists(self, **conditions) -> bool:
        """Check whether any records match the given conditions.
        
        Args:
            conditions: Column-value pairs to filter the existence check.
            
        Returns:
            bool: True if at least one matching record exists, False otherwise.
        """
        count = self._db.session.query(self._model_class).filter_by(**conditions).count()
        return count > 0

    def count_entries(self) -> int:
        """Return total number of records in the table.
        
        Returns:
            int: Total count of records.
        """
        return self._db.session.query(self._model_class).count()

    # Helper method to support deletion and other operations requiring multiple results
    def find_all_filtered(self, **kwargs) -> List[BaseModel]:
        """Internal helper to get all records matching filters."""
        return self._db.session.query(self._model_class).filter_by(**kwargs).all()

# Process NREL polymer data file and extract specific properties into JSON format

import sys
import os
import json

def main(arguments):
    # Determine paths and filenames based on command-line arguments
    base_dir = "/path/to/user/Documents/MDF"
    input_file = "NREL_polymer_export.txt"
    output_file = "NREL_polymer_output.txt"
    
    if len(arguments) == 1:
        base_dir = os.path.dirname(arguments[0])
        input_file = os.path.basename(arguments[0])
        output_file = arguments[1] if len(arguments) > 1 else "NREL_polymer_output.txt"
    
    # Construct full file path and process the file
    full_path = construct_file_path(base_dir, input_file)
    records = load_and_parse_data(full_path)
    
    # Write results to output file
    try:
        with open(output_file, "w") as writer:
            for item in records:
                json_line = json.dumps(item)
                print(json_line)
                writer.write(json_line + "\n")
    except IOError:
        print("No valid records found!")
    
    print("COMPLETED")

def construct_file_path(directory, filename):
    """Build a proper file path ensuring correct separator usage."""
    if directory.endswith("/"):
        return directory + filename
    else:
        return f"{directory}/{filename}"

def load_and_parse_data(filepath):
    """
    Extract specified fields from NREL data file.
    
    Target fields include:
    - gap_extrapolated (Extrapolated Gap)
    - delta_homo (HOMO difference)
    - sum_f_osc (Oscillator strength sum)
    - delta_optical_lumo (Optical LUMO difference)
    - delta_lumo (LUMO difference)
    - spectral_overlap (Spectral overlap)
    - functional/basis (Functional basis)
    - homo_extrapolated (Extrapolated HOMO)
    - common_tag (Common identifier)
    - optical_lumo_extrapolated (Extrapolated Optical LUMO)
    - lumo_extrapolated (Extrapolated LUMO)
    
    :param filepath: Full path to the input data file
    :return: List of dictionaries containing extracted data
    """
    if not os.path.exists(filepath):
        print(f"Error: File '{filepath}' not found.")
        return []
    
    try:
        with open(filepath, 'r') as reader:
            lines = reader.readlines()
        
        if not lines:
            return []
            
        headers = lines[0].strip().split()
        data_records = []
        
        for idx, line in enumerate(lines[1:], start=2):
            cleaned_line = line.strip()
            if not cleaned_line:
                continue
                
            values = cleaned_line.split()
            
            if len(values) == len(headers):
                record = dict(zip(headers, values))
                data_records.append(record)
            else:
                print(f"Line {idx}: Column count mismatch. Expected {len(headers)}, got {len(values)}")
                
        return data_records
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading file: {e}")
        return []

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else [])

# Load preprocessed statements and analyze evidence sources
from util import pklload
from collections import defaultdict
import indra.tools.assemble_corpus as ac

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # Load cached Statements just before going into the model
    stmts = pklload('pysb_stmts')
    
    # Initialize a dictionary to track source combinations
    source_combinations = defaultdict(int)
    
    # Process each statement to identify its evidence sources
    for stmt in stmts:
        # Extract unique source APIs from evidence, sort them for consistency
        sources = tuple(sorted(set(ev.source_api for ev in stmt.evidence)))
        source_combinations[sources] += 1
    
    # Initialize counters for different source categories
    database_only_count = 0
    reader_only_count = 0
    combined_sources_count = 0
    
    # Define known database and reader source categories
    database_sources = {'bel', 'biopax', 'phosphosite', 'signor'}
    reader_sources = {'reach', 'trips', 'sparser', 'r3'}
    
    # Categorize statements based on their source composition
    for source_tuple, count in source_combinations.items():
        sources_set = set(source_tuple)
        
        db_intersection = sources_set & database_sources
        reader_intersection = sources_set & reader_sources
        
        if db_intersection and reader_intersection:
            combined_sources_count += count
        elif db_intersection and not reader_intersection:
            database_only_count += count
        elif reader_intersection and not db_intersection:
            reader_only_count += count
    
    # Print source combination statistics sorted by frequency
    for sources, count in sorted(source_combinations.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
        print(sources, count)

import unittest
from math import pi, fmod

class AngleNormalizationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tolerance = 1e-6
    
    def test_angle_in_first_quadrant_remains_unchanged(self):
        angle_deg = 45
        angle_rad = angle_deg * pi / 180.0
        result = normalize_angle(angle_rad)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(angle_rad, result, delta=self.tolerance)
    
    def test_negative_angle_converted_to_positive_equivalent(self):
        angle_rad = -pi / 2
        expected = 3 * pi / 2
        result = normalize_angle(angle_rad)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(expected, result, delta=self.tolerance)
    
    def test_full_circle_maps_to_zero(self):
        angle_rad = 2 * pi
        expected = 0.0
        result = normalize_angle(angle_rad)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(expected, result, delta=self.tolerance)
    
    def test_large_positive_angle_reduced_correctly(self):
        angle_deg = 370.5
        angle_rad = angle_deg * pi / 180.0
        expected_deg = 10.5
        expected_rad = expected_deg * pi / 180.0
        result = normalize_angle(angle_rad)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(expected_rad, result, delta=self.tolerance)
    
    def test_large_negative_angle_reduced_correctly(self):
        angle_deg = -370
        angle_rad = angle_deg * pi / 180.0
        expected_deg = 350
        expected_rad = expected_deg * pi / 180.0
        result = normalize_angle(angle_rad)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(expected_rad, result, delta=self.tolerance)

# Implementation of the normalized angle function
def normalize_angle(angle):
    # Normalize angle to be within [0, 2π)
    normalized = fmod(angle, 2 * pi)
    if normalized < 0:
        normalized += 2 * pi
    return normalized

def swap_pairs(elements):

    # Swap elements at even and odd positions
    for i in range(0, len(result) - 1, 2):
        result[i], result[i + 1] = result[i + 1], result[i]
    return result

import numpy as np
from neurons import spiking, plotting, tools

def simulate_jeffress_model(output_gain):
    # Define neuron count and simulation duration
    total_neurons = 180 * 3 + 2
    sim_duration = 300
    
    # Configure axonal delay profile
    delay_profile = np.zeros(total_neurons)
    delay_profile[1:181] = np.linspace(0, 100, 180)
    delay_profile[182:362] = np.linspace(100, 0, 180)
    
    # Initialize spiking model with specified parameters
    neural_model = spiking.SRM_X(
        neurons=total_neurons,
        threshold=np.ones(total_neurons),
        t_current=np.full(total_neurons, 45),
        t_membrane=np.full(total_neurons, 50),
        eta_reset=np.full(total_neurons, 5.0),
        ax_delay=delay_profile,
        simulation_window_size=500
    )
    
    # Build synaptic weight matrix
    synapse_matrix = np.zeros((total_neurons, total_neurons))
    
    # Input layer connections
    synapse_matrix[0, 1:181] = 1.0
    synapse_matrix[181, 182:361] = 1.0
    
    # Inter-layer to output layer connections
    identity_block = np.eye(180)
    synapse_matrix[1:181, 362:542] = output_gain * identity_block
    synapse_matrix[182:362, 362:542] = output_gain * identity_block
    
    # Generate input spike patterns with timing offset
    input_spike_pattern = np.zeros((total_neurons, sim_duration), dtype=bool)
    input_spike_pattern[0, [50, 55, 60]] = True
    input_spike_pattern[181, [0, 5, 10]] = True
    
    # Run simulation step-by-step
    for time_step in range(sim_duration):
        neural_model.check_spikes(input_spike_pattern, synapse_matrix, time_step)
    
    # Output analysis results
    print("output gain:", output_gain)
    print("spike counts in output layer:")
    print(np.sum(input_spike_pattern, axis=1)[362:])

def compute_classification_score(label, features):
    """Run classification across plugins and compute average confidence score."""
    global _plugin_instances
    if _plugin_instances is None:
        _initialize_plugin_system()
    
    score_accumulator = 0.0
    active_count = 0
    
    for instance in _plugin_instances:
        result = instance.classify(label, features)
        if result is not None:
            active_count += 1

import base64
import xmltodict
import json
import colorama
from .safe_print import safe_print
from .exceptions import SAMLAssertionParseError

def parse_assertion(assertion: str) -> list:
    # Initialize empty list to store AWS roles
    aws_roles = []
    
    # Decode and parse the SAML assertion XML
    decoded_assertion = base64.b64decode(assertion)
    parsed_response = xmltodict.parse(decoded_assertion)
    
    # Try different namespace prefixes for SAML response elements
    saml2p_ns = 'saml2p:Response'
    samlp_ns = 'samlp:Response'
    
    if saml2p_ns in parsed_response:
        # Handle SAML 2.0 format
        assertion_data = parsed_response[saml2p_ns].get('saml2:Assertion', {})
        attribute_statement = assertion_data.get('saml2:AttributeStatement', {})
        attributes_list = attribute_statement.get('saml2:Attribute', [])
        value_key = 'saml2:AttributeValue'
    elif samlp_ns in parsed_response:
        # Handle older SAML format
        assertion_data = parsed_response[samlp_ns].get('saml:Assertion', {})
        attribute_statement = assertion_data.get('saml:AttributeStatement', {})
        attributes_list = attribute_statement.get('saml:Attribute', [])
        value_key = 'saml:AttributeValue'
    else:
        # No valid SAML response found
        raise SAMLAssertionParseError()
    
    # Check if attributes exist
    if not attributes_list:
        raise SAMLAssertionParseError()
    
    # Process each attribute to find role attributes
    for attr in attributes_list:
        if attr.get('@Name') == 'https://aws.amazon.com/SAML/Attributes/Role':
            # Extract role values from the attribute
            role_values = attr.get(value_key, [])
            if isinstance(role_values, list):
                for role_entry in role_values:
                    aws_roles.append(role_entry.get('#text'))
            else:
                # Handle case where it's a single value (not in a list)
                aws_roles.append(role_values.get('#text'))
    
    return aws_roles

    )

        '--ip',
        '-i',
        required=True,
        help='IP name in snake_case format (e.g., uart)'
    )
    cli_parser.add_argument(
        '--peripheral',
        '-p',
        required=True,
        help='Human-readable peripheral name for documentation (e.g., UART)'
    )
    cli_parser.add_argument(
        '--handle-param',
        '-a',
        default='handle',
        help='Custom parameter name to use instead of "handle" (default: handle)'
    )
    cli_parser.add_argument(
        '--template',
        '-t',
        type=Path,
        default=default_template_path,
        help='Path to the Mako template file (default: dif_template.h.tpl)'
    )
    cli_parser.add_argument(
        '--output',
        '-o',
        type=Path,
        help='Output path for generated header; defaults to dif_<ip>.h'
    )
    
    parsed_args = cli_parser.parse_args()
    
    # Process naming conventions
    ip_snake_case = parsed_args.ip
    ip_camel_case = ''.join(word.capitalize() for word in ip_snake_case.split('_'))
    ip_upper_case = ip_snake_case.upper()
    
    periph_name_lower = parsed_args.peripheral
    # Capitalize only the first character, leave rest unchanged
    periph_name_upper = periph_name_lower[0].upper() + periph_name_lower[1:]
    
    custom_handle_param = parsed_args.handle_param
    
    # Load and render the template
    with parsed_args.template.open('r') as template_file:
        raw_template = template_file.read()
    
    rendered_header = Template(raw_template).render(
        ip_snake=ip_snake_case,
        ip_camel=ip_camel_case,
        ip_upper=ip_upper_case,
        periph_lower=periph_name_lower,
        periph_upper=periph_name_upper,
        handle=custom_handle_param,
    )
    
    # Determine output file path
    output_path = parsed_args.output or dif_directory / f"dif_{ip_snake_case}.h"
    
    # Write the generated header
    with output_path.open('w') as output_file:
        output_file.write(rendered_header)
    
    print(f"Header file successfully generated at {str(output_path)}.")

# Calculate electrical power and current relationships

from UliEngineering.EngineerIO import normalize_numeric
from UliEngineering.Units import Unit

__all__ = ["compute_current_from_power_voltage", "compute_power_from_current_voltage"]

def compute_current_from_power_voltage(power_value="25 W", voltage_value="230 V") -> Unit("A"):
    """
    Given a device's power (or RMS power) and the voltage (or RMS voltage)
    it operates on, determine the resulting current draw.
    """
    normalized_power = normalize_numeric(power_value)
    normalized_voltage = normalize_numeric(voltage_value)
    return normalized_power / normalized_voltage

def compute_power_from_current_voltage(current_value="1.0 A", voltage_value="230 V") -> Unit("W"):
    """
    Given a device's current (or RMS current) and the voltage (or RMS voltage)
    it operates on, determine its power consumption.
    """
    normalized_current = normalize_numeric(current_value)
    normalized_voltage = normalize_numeric(voltage_value)
    return normalized_current * normalized_voltage

def peninsula_simulation(grid_basename, particle_count):
    """Simulate particle flow around an idealised Peninsula
    :param grid_basename: Basename of the input grid file set
    :param particle_count: Number of particles to initialise"""
    
    # Load grid data from file set
    ocean_grid = NEMOGrid(grid_basename)
    
    # Create and position particles along a specific latitude range
    initial_particles = []
    for idx in range(particle_count):
        lat_offset = idx * ocean_grid.lat_u.valid_max / particle_count + 0.45 / 1.852 / 60.
        new_particle = Particle(x=3 / 1.852 / 60., y=lat_offset)
        ocean_grid.add_particle(new_particle)
        initial_particles.append(new_particle)
    
    print("Initial particle configurations:")

    # Run simulation for 24 hours with fixed time step
    total_time = 86400.0  # seconds

    for step in range(steps):

# Check language coverage against Unicode script subsets

import sys
from collections import defaultdict
try:
    import gflanguages
except Exception:
    import pytest
    pytest.skip(
        "Coverage test requires gflanguages to be installed",
        allow_module_level=True,
    )

from glyphsets.codepoints import CodepointsInSubset
from fontTools.unicodedata.Scripts import NAMES
import unicodedata
import warnings

# Special codepoints that should always be considered available
ESSENTIAL_CODEPOINTS = {0x2010, 0xA}

def verify_language_coverage():
    languages_data = gflanguages.LoadLanguages()
    missing_codepoints = defaultdict(set)
    affected_languages = defaultdict(list)
    has_errors = False
    
    for lang_name, lang_metadata in languages_data.items():
        # Extract codepoints used in sample text
        used_codepoints = set()
        for field, sample_text in lang_metadata.sample_text.ListFields():
            for char in sample_text:
                used_codepoints.add(ord(char))
        
        # Parse language and script from name
        try:
            lang, script = lang_name.split("_")
        except ValueError:
            continue
            
        # Skip if script not recognized
        if script not in NAMES:
            continue
            
        # Convert script name to file format
        script_filename = NAMES[script].lower().replace(" ", "-").replace("_", "-")
        
        # Get codepoints defined for this script subset
        subset_codepoints = set(CodepointsInSubset(script_filename, unique_glyphs=False))
        subset_codepoints |= ESSENTIAL_CODEPOINTS
        
        # Check if subset is empty (no glyphs defined)
        if not subset_codepoints:
            warnings.warn(f"No codepoints defined for {lang_name}")
            has_errors = True
            continue
            
        # Find missing codepoints
        missing = used_codepoints - subset_codepoints
        if missing:
            has_errors = True
            missing_codepoints[script_filename].update(missing)
            affected_languages[script_filename].append(lang_name)
    
    # Report errors if any found
    if not has_errors:
        return
        
    for script_name, missing_cps in missing_codepoints.items():
        print(
            f"\n{script_name} is missing the following codepoints to render samples "
            f"in {', '.join(affected_languages[script_name])}:\n",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        for cp in sorted(missing_cps):
            char = chr(cp)
            char_name = unicodedata.name(char, "UNNAMED")
            print(
                f"U+{cp:04X}  {char} {char_name}", 
                file=sys.stderr
            )
    
    assert False, "Language coverage verification failed"

# Run the verification
verify_language_coverage()

# Import necessary modules for execution, logging, and async handling
import runpy
import os
import sys
import asyncio
import traceback
import pylp
import pylp.cli.logger as logger
from pylp.utils.paths import make_readable_path

# Execute a pylpfile with specified tasks
def execute_pylp_file(file_path, task_names):
    # Convert path to readable format for logging
    display_path = make_readable_path(file_path)
    
    # Check if the pylpfile exists
    if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
        logger.log(logger.red("Unable to access pylpfile "), logger.magenta(display_path))
        sys.exit(-1)
    else:
        logger.log("Found pylpfile ", logger.magenta(display_path))
    
    # Attempt to execute the pylpfile
    try:
        runpy.run_path(file_path, None, "pylpfile")
    except Exception as error:
        traceback.print_exc(stream=sys.stdout)
        logger.log(logger.red("\nAn error occurred while executing the pylpfile"))
        sys.exit(-1)
    
    # Initialize each requested task
    for task_name in task_names:
        pylp.start(task_name)
    
    # Run event loop until all tasks complete
    event_loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    event_loop.run_until_complete(terminate_after_tasks(event_loop))

# Asynchronous function to wait for all running tasks to finish
async def terminate_after_tasks(loop):
    from pylp.lib.tasks import running
    
    if running:
        futures = [runner.future for runner in running]
        await asyncio.wait(futures)
